title: Joe Thuney on staying hungry and continuing to improve | Press Conference
text: So, it's kind of stinking to see a guy like the N guy go down. Obviously, you don't know what happened, but when you have not padded practices and guys are moving fast and accidents sort of happen. >> Yeah, absolutely. Kyle, can't say enough good things about him. You know, hopefully it's nothing too crazy significant. Um, but you know, football is just football's football. It's tough, but uh hope he's all right. >> What What did you appreciate about him during his season last year? >> Yeah, he's great. I mean, he's came in just worked really hard, really detailed in the playbook, you know. Um, runs so hard, plays hard for his teammates. Um, great guy you want to block for, great in pass protection. Uh, really a great player. >> Made it back out there today. What's your reaction to a guy that ahead of schedule? >> I know. Can you believe it? Yeah, it's awesome. Just um, you know, credit to him, the staff here, trainers, weight staff, you know, everybody. Just um, you just want to see it's great to see him back on the field. you know, I'm not who knows, you know, what the timet will be, but um you just great to see him moving in football positions again, helmet on. Um you know, he's um he had another great year last year and uh yeah, just it's cool to see him out there. >> What did you appreciate about the way he ended the season before the injury? >> Yeah. Um yeah, I mean, I still can't believe he got off the field on his own power, you know, it's pretty remarkable in that situation. Um, but another guy came in as rookie, worked really hard, you know, in his playbook all the time, great teammate, you know, um, just, you know, just great guy, guy went out, um, and, uh, yeah, so so it's awesome to see him put the work in the whole offseason, get back try and get back in position to play again and, um, yeah, really happy for him. >> How would you approach the left tackle competition going on next to you, just in terms of how it's affected you just rotating or in ways that you're trying to help them? Yeah, I mean, um, there's just there's a lot of great guys over there, you know, regardless who's in there and try and, you know, try and communicate as well as I can. Uh, you know, trying to get the run fits, you know, as consistent as I can, so it's feels the same for everybody. And, um, then, you know, just just trying to be on the same page with what each play, you know, playing right next to them. And, um, you know, but they're all great. They all, um, you know, working really hard and, um, you know, so half the time, you know, it's pretty tired. You don't hardly realize like, oh, hey, he's next, you know. So, um, but they're all, you know, they're all doing a great job. >> Sure. You've been, uh, getting accolades dating back to last season, recently voted, uh, top interior lineman. Um, at this stage in your career, do you, uh, take time to savor those? And what's kind of your thought about this stage of your career for you? >> Yeah. Um, you know, it's obviously really it's it's always humbling and exciting when you see your name, you know, attached to kind those kind of things, but at the end of the day, I I just I'm really concerned with how the team does and just want to start season 1 and know and um just really um just love playing football still. want to be out there with the guys, you know, it's um you know, it's what it's all about. And um just want to try and contribute to the Chicago Bears and um you know, it's there's it's a it's not just an individual, you know, I feel like there's so many pieces around me, you know, whether it's the other alignment, the quarterbacks, running backs hitting the hole well, you know, the play calls being great, receivers getting open. So, it's I mean I'm just a small part in a big machine and um just want to do my part the best I can and um you know just love being out there playing with the guys. >> Joe, you think you're a better player now than you were in your 20s even though you know physically you probably can't maintain what you had in your 20s. >> Yeah. Um yeah, it's uh you know, just I I think I um obviously like you said, it's different, you know, as you get older, you know, get gain more experience, but you know, maybe physically um you know, your body's different than you know, when you are at 23. And um but I try and just um still try and maintain a high standard and try and you do the best I can every play and um just try and uh you know, hold myself to the high standard still. >> What do you think of Jeter, your passer? Yeah, he was great. Um, really cool to hear him speak. Um, great lessons, you know, a guy who's so successful, such a great leader and, um, it's awesome when people can come in like that and give, you know, their opinions and thoughts and, uh, learned a lot from him. >> You played for contenders pretty much your whole career. Uh, does playing for a contending team with the Bears fuel you to keep going or do you kind of have a set uh, career span in your mind? >> No. Yeah, I mean um I think you know all competitors want to, you know, be in the be in the tournament, be in the final round and, you know, want to try and compete, you know, for um to go as far as possible. So, um I still, you know, love, you know, working to get wins, you know, and trying to, you know, put together, um, good seasons, but, um, I I still just love playing and I love competing and I feel great being a part of the Bears, you know, a lot of, uh, great things going on and just want to contribute what I can, but um, yeah. >> You've been a part of winning programs obviously everywhere you've been. What in your experience when success occurs allows it to keep going? Yeah, I think um I think just uh you know guys working for the team for the good of the whole. um you know, people being selfless, people doing what's best for the team and being able to sustain that, you know, day after day, week after week, month after month and um you know, I think um Ben's done a great job. um you just setting the standard high and the standard is the standard and you know it's all about the team success and I think that's just uh you just we just want to play together win together you know and it's a team game ultimate team game and um yeah >> those types of things and the quarterbacks and the head coaches you played with how much are those guys an engine of what you've just talked about? Yeah, I think um I think kind of the message kind of been this says said in different ways but kind of remains the same just you know it's all about the team and um how everyone contributes everyone you know does what they can to the best of their ability and um you know the sum of the parts are greater than the the parts individually. So um you know this it's a it's a beautiful game and it's awesome. >> You talk about the sum of the parts. >> How do you see your role has changed from last year to this year? Maybe it hasn't at all as far as you know what your role is on this team. Yeah, just trying to um set a great example, be a leader, you know, if um played in a lot of different situations, a lot of different teammates and um you know, I think um you know, when guys approach me or ask or or talk about different things that happen throughout the season, you the ups and downs, trying to um you keep a steady course and um um but at the end of the day, just trying, you know, um be the best lift guard I can be, be the best offensive lineman I can be, um and help the O line room as much as I can, and um you know, helping the offense and the team. But um just trying to to do the best that I can. >> Joe, you have this deep perspective from being in the league so long and from success and things like that. What what does last year mean to you in terms of coming to a new place, coming in at uh at your age and having it go as well as it did for you and for the team? Yeah, I think um you know it was special seeing you know so many videos after the game of you know we had a lot of close games and wins and seeing families hugging, crying together and you know Chicago Bears are such an iconic franchise and um you know it's great the Chicago Bears being back in the playoffs and you know be able to get in the playoffs, get a win um win the NFC North um you know so it's just um but there's still more things to achieve and um you know obviously there are a lot cool moments last year, but I don't think anybody in this building is satisfied. You know, I don't think anybody's, you know, relaxing on that or resting on that. And I think um that's that's what's so cool is there's still a very very strong, you know, burning hunger and desire to push push more and keep going, keep improving. Um so there's a lot lot still left to do. >> Joe, uh Press was talking earlier about how the pre-nap operations are crisper and that's part because the players are taking ownership. Does that happen organically or do veterans like yourself help make that happen? >> Yeah, I think just um everyone being kind of a lot of people being back for the second year and the offense just kind of being more familiar with the terminology, vernacular and um you know kind of the how things go and um and then yeah, I think just holding each other to accountable, holding each other to a high standard. Um you know, just [clears throat] just um you know, we have high expectations and try and hold each other to that. Joe, given your your past with Garrett, how do you describe what he brings to that position that makes him special? >> Yeah, he's a great guy. Um, you know, it's um it's crazy after all these years being back together now. And um but you know, he's um he's really smart. He communicates so well. He's athletic, he's strong, you know, um so he does a lot of really things really well and he's uh done a lot of work to, you know, catch himself up on the offense. um all the terms we use.

title: Press Taylor says joint practices are a great opportunity to prove worth | Press Conference
text: Will you get to have dinner with your brother or anything this week? >> Uh I think we'll there'll be an opportunity for us to get together at some point. We'll see, but we'll see how it goes. >> What What's the plan at uh left tackle for for this week? >> Um we'll see about, you know, getting everybody back healthy, and see where where Braxton is, if he comes back healthy, and and what his availability looks like, and then we'll kind of go from there. We'll see um what the week entails, what we want to do. I think the the big mission kind of has just been throw a lot of people in there, give a lot of people an opportunity, and see where we go from there. >> But pretty soon you have to start removing people from the competition now, right? To get >> That would be the goal. I mean, as soon as we can make a decision, we feel clear and confident that this is the person to go forward with, we'd love to be able to do that. But until then, we'll let the process play out. >> What the film show of the What the film show of the two guys yesterday? >> I thought um you know, we had a good plan for getting both. I think they got I think one of them got 30, one of them got 34 snaps, and you know, they start with their starters, so it's a good opportunity um to see them against Jared Verse first play the game. So, I think both guys so showed some positive traits that you wanted to see from them. Um it wasn't perfect. It wasn't as clean as we'd love it to be going forward, and that's kind of why they're still continue to be in open competition for the position. Um but I think there were some encouraging things we continue to teach from and coach from and grow from. >> As if Braxton makes a smooth return to action, what's the target for him the next two to three weeks just to show you that he's where he needs to be? >> I think these joint practices will be huge for that, cuz it's kind of an opportunity where you know, we'll go into it at times with intentionally not helping those guys on the side, where that's different from a game week. You know, you you face a dynamic pass rush on one side, you may provide presence with a tight end. Well, in these situations, in these controlled environments where your quarterback's got the red jersey on, it's a little bit more of an opportunity that let's go see you one-on-one with some guys. It's a couple different pass rushers you haven't seen. So, I think it's a great opportunity over these next two weeks for everybody in that role to really kind of prove their worth for us. >> If he keeps making kind of plays seemingly every day. What have you seen from him and are you I don't want to say surprised, but what are your thoughts on his emergence in the game as well? >> Yeah, he's done a great job and it like you said, he continue to produces produce with the opportunities he's been given. Um, you know, you got to put wins on tape. He had a contested catch on the sideline over there. He had a couple other plays. He did a good job blocking. We had a big third down conversion on a run early with Roshan where he shows up and he's blocking the safety. Comes and springs us for our longest run of the day. Um, so he he put a lot of good things on tape and he's continued to do that. So, um, that's really all you can ask for for those guys that they make the most of their opportunities and he's continued to do that and I think that's why you see more and more opportunities go his way. >> You talked to us uh maybe like a week ago or something and you weren't pleased with some of the pre-snap snap stuff. Where are you guys at with that now? >> It was it was much cleaner in the game than it really had been through practice. So, that was good to see. Um, and I think that that kind of comes and goes with training camp as you're trying to jump the count a little bit on guys that also know your cadence and so it when you're competing against yourselves, um, so that makes it tough and I thought it was a much cleaner operation in the game. There's still things we need to clean up. I think there are things that we kind of got away with even at the game, um, that you want to see go smoother. So, we have a lot of room to grow still there. >> Setting [snorts] aside the game, what how's it going with the first string offense? >> They've done a good job. They're they're getting better and that's kind of what we expect. You know, we we're continuing to challenge the quarterbacks with cadence. We want them to, um, have variety in the way that they communicate at the line of scrimmage and change things up and, you know, we change pictures. We're getting now into the part of camp where, you know, our defense does certain things and the quarterbacks may see it and recognize it and we want them to get to something that maybe is not in the call. So, that changes the flow of communication. So, that's something you're seeing in the last probably in the last week that's popped up a lot more of opportunities for that and I think we've handled that pretty well so far, but that's something we can continue to grow as we got, you know, these next three, four weeks before week one. >> How often how often do you marvel over Joe Flacco >> Often. Often. It And it's honestly, you have to go back and be like, "Oh, I got to remember to watch Joe." Because nothing pops. Joe didn't get beat. Joe You just almost forget that that those two guys were playing cuz Joe just eliminates somebody instantly. You got to go back and really appreciate what he just did there. Um you know, he's got really really strong hands. That's the one thing we talk about. When he gets his hands on guys, that the the rush kind of stops. Like it just or the movement stops. So, it's really impressive with what he's able to do. Um but it's also impressive like the professionalism he plays with. The other day we were just joking. We're in a walk-through to get ready for Cleveland. So, the guys that are going to play in the game are walking through. Obviously, Joe's not playing, so he's on the scout team defense. And he's out there running around, goofing off, like blitzing as a nickel. And Case Keenum are sitting there like, "This guy's won six Super Bowls. And he's over here having the time of his life playing scout team nickel in a walk-through right now." And so, just you appreciate the professionalism, the look he's It's important to him to provide a good look for the young players, to kind of pour into them a little bit, and it's really cool to see. That was awesome. Uh anytime you get, you know, kind of from the era I grew up in, that's greatness. Walking in the building and the the coolest thing he had was just his perspective on everything of how, you know, he talked about he didn't ever think about failure. He always thought about even in He's known as being one of the most clutch players of our generation. Well, he talked about, you know, when I had an opportunity for it, I went back to the last time I had success. I didn't think about the time I failed in this moment. He went He talked about going back to being a sophomore in high school and scoring a game-winning basket. Like that's what he's thinking about when he's in game seven of the World Series up to bat in a critical moment. He's thinking of the time I succeeded at this time. So, I just thought that was really cool, his perspective and sharing with it. He seemed like a pretty down-to-earth guy. Um his life's probably a lot different than a lot of our lives, but to see that humility and just the personality that he had was really cool. >> You mentioned your generation. Do you think that maybe the coaches were I don't want to say more impressed. >> I think so. I think probably we were. We made sure to show highlight when it started of kind of who he was, his accomplishments just because some of these guys may not have watched Derek Jeter play. Um, but I think when they kind of saw the accomplishments rolling across the screen, saw his highlights, and then hear the guy talk, you have an appreciation for it. >> Coach, some of the uh some of the uh guys' performances obviously uh down the depth chart like Ja'Mycal Hasty, [snorts] Sam Williams. What were your assessments of their games? And what are some coaching points from them uh from that preseason opener? >> Yeah, I thought some good things showed. Um, you know, I thought Sam made his presence felt in the run game, which is something we wanted to see. I think there's still opportunities to grow in the pass game. You know, he had a a ball come his way that we would have probably like to see a better ball, but we talked through Sam the coaching points of how we could potentially run the route a little bit better. Um, and that's something that's just going to continue to grow and expand in his game. And the same thing with Ja'Mycal Hasty, you're seeing a confident Ja'Mycal Hasty, which last year I I don't think Ja'Mycal Hasty has ever struggled with his confidence, but you know, you saw him make plays and kind of fly onto the scene last year. Well, now more's expected of you. So, are you going to be able to produce when there's more expected of you? And I think we're we're very happy with um, the way Ja'Mycal Hasty continues to grow every single day and approaches his craft. >> Has Caleb shown you enough to where that he's mastered the system enough to where you don't need to see him in a scenario where he can actually take a hit like preseason? >> Well, I don't know if I'd say that. I mean, I think he's getting closer and closer every single day to improving in his mastery of the system. I I don't know if he's ever going to get there. I don't know that anybody ever will. I think us as coaches, we continue every day to learn a little bit more about the system and where it can go and how we can evolve it and grow. And so, I think all our players are getting better at it and making it their own. It's always going to evolve, but I think in terms of him playing in a preseason game, I think that's kind of a case-by-case basis. Like, I don't think we're going to make any definitive statements today on what he's going to do in game two or game three because we want to see what the week entails. If we get some good work and we're confident, then maybe they won't play. If we, you know, want to see a little bit more or change the situation or the dynamics, then we can reserve the right to make that decision when the time comes. >> Independent of last season's foot issues, what have been your assessments of Rome's camp here in the last three weeks? >> I thought I think Rome's done a good job. I think I mentioned it back when if he hadn't said anything about his foot being different, I don't think you would have noticed because of what you're saying. You're seeing the speed down the field. I think you're seeing a little bit even more detail in his route show up as we've gone. And that's to be expected. It's year two. He's heard all the coaching points on this. He understands where he's supposed to be, when he's supposed to be there. You see the explosion in his game. You see the contested catchability that he has. And I think we've increased our giving him those opportunities as well. You know, we've made it a point of emphasis to try to push the ball down field in some contested go goals because that's obviously a strength of his. That's something we didn't feature much as a coaching staff last year. So, to add to our offense and what we can do and experiment with certain things, we've we've given him some of those opportunities. He's made his share his fair share of plays on those. So, that's encouraging. >> That one by the goal post in the back of the end zone that one day, do you have any feedback on on that play that he made there? >> No, I mean, I think there's been a number of those I can think of off the top of my head and through camp, whether it's one-on-ones or team settings that he's able to make contested catches. And again, that's something that goes back to his college tape that was a strength of his. So, we're just trying to kind of lean in and see how that fits our offense. >> What were some of your takeaways with the interior guys who did play yesterday, particularly Logan and Caleb? >> Yeah, those guys got a lot of work. They got a lot of reps. You know, obviously, we've had some injuries in the the depth of our interior, so we knew those guys, some of them were going to play multiple positions inside and get 60 to 70 reps. And so, I think you're encouraged with what they were able to do. It's a very different setting for those guys. You know, they go from getting three plays at the tail end of a a practice period four or five times a day to all of a sudden you're playing 70 plays and you know, a guy like Carl Herbig's playing left guard, moving to center. Um, at a different speed. You know, you're seeing a different front, different players. So, I think there's a lot to be encouraged with and I'm excited to see where those guy where those guys go in joint practices and as as well as preseason, too. >> Last few games in particular, what's just the uh the overall like clean operation of the offense? Um, if you go back to last year, there was multiple times Ben went public with some frustration, probably trying to send a message, light a fire. Uh, he just seemed relatively calm, at least for Ben >> Yeah. >> compared about that. How different does it look to you? >> Um, I think you see a lot more glimpses of what we expect it to be. And I think that's the biggest thing is everybody knows what what the standard is, what it looks like, what our pre-snap operation looks like. And I think talking with our guys, they feel it. They feel what it's like to come out of the huddle with clarity, conviction in what we're doing, how we operate before the ball's ever snapped. You know, we we shift in motion as much as anybody in the league. So, all the moving parts pre-snap and then taking advantage of our cadence, the presentation of the of the formation, the motion, things like that. I think there's a lot of ownership in that, which is really what you're trying to get. When the players own the pre-snap process, it's going to take off. And when when we're able to function at a high level before the ball's ever put in play, we're in a pretty good position once the ball's in in play because of kind of all the moving parts and variety we present as an offense. >> Most memorable game you played against your brother, whether you were a kid or whatever. >> Ooh. Uh, I think in the NFL, the most memorable one for me was probably 2017 playing the Rams. We went out there late in the year. That's the game Carson Wentz tore his ACL. They were a good team. I think that was their second year where they were playing pretty well on offense and we were able to win that game. Just kind of the the stakes at the time is week 11, 12, 13, something like that. It was a big win for us. I think we clinched the playoffs at that time. That was pretty big. Um in terms of being a kid, I don't know. There's a number of battles in the front yard that I can think of that probably ended with me losing and getting upset. They were most of the time, you know, he's 5 years older than me, so it wasn't always fair, but we I remember a lot of times of him dragging me to go outside and play catch, and I didn't want to, and I ended up sitting in the front yard, and he's just throwing a ball at me as far as he could. That was our idea of playing catch, I guess, for a long time. We played a lot We had like a 10-yd grass area in the front yard, and we'd play punt return. So, I'm I'm, say, eight, and he's 13, and it was him throwing the ball as high as he could, and I had to look up and catch it, and we're 10 yd apart. So, he'd just smoke me while I'm trying to catch a punt, basically, but that was the gist of our games, for the most part, when it was just he and I. that's what I look forward to >> [laughter] >> forward to getting after him, if I can, out there, so we'll see. >> Something something characteristic of a little brother. >> Yeah, exactly. That's That's how it goes, but >> All right. Thank you, guys.

title: A cinematic recap of the Broncos' preseason win over the Falcons | Sights & Sounds
text: Good evening everyone, welcome to Mercedes-Benz Stadium here in Atlanta, Georgia, where everything is ready for the preseason football game between the visiting Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons. Excited for the start of the preseason, friends.  After a great year last year, the Broncos made it all the way to the AFC Championship Game. There's excitement everywhere; Broncos fans are ready for the start of the season. Stidham towards the far side, the pass is complete.  It's a 15- yard gain for number 13, Cam Bryan. Stidham receives the shotgun cross, steps forward and launches a deep ball for Sutton, who jumps. Courtland makes the reception inside the five-yard line, all the way to the one-yard line.  First goal for Denver.  40 yards, from Stidham to Sutton.  He outplayed Mike Hughes on the play and looked like an NBA power forward. The fullback in formation I, Penisini receives his second carry of the series and goes all the way to the end zone.  Touchdown for Denver. Adam Pernish's 1-yard touchdown run .  And the Broncos travel 69 yards. Third and 15, short lateral pass.  It gives the clearer a little more space. Receive the cross, look to the left, throw to the left, throw towards Gordon.  He raises a hand and secures the ball against his body for a first down catch at the 43-yard line. Here comes the pressure.  Loafer touches it and throws the ball to the ground. He receives the cross, pressure from four men in the final zone, he throws to the center of the field and is caught.  Ingram breaks a tackle.  He carries the ball to the 30-yard line. He passes it out to the left side, Joan Coleman breaks free, turns to avoid a tackle and, like an unstoppable force, charges through Atlanta Falcons players to the 37-yard line, maybe the 38 . Stidham fakes, stays in the pocket, moves, throws a laser pass to a wide- open receiver inside the 30-yard line. Nice work by Troy Franklin.  Center, placement, kick high enough, and it's good.  Look to the left, turn right, throw the ball and it will be intercepted.  Ball intercepted , the pass was left behind.  That's Riley Moss.  Moss with the interception, and it was a difficult one as well.  Stidham with a feint.  In trouble, he throws a short safety pass.  It's Jalil McLaughlin , who walks into the end zone for a Denver touchdown. 5-yard reception. Shotgun cross for Rypien, looks left, shoots left, ball deflected and intercepted out of bounds and down the wing.  It was Kareem Reed who deflected the ball, and Jon A. Bostic will walk into the end zone with a touchdown for Denver .  And final score from Mercedes-Benz Stadium here in Atlanta, the Broncos in their first preseason game on the road beat the Atlanta Falcons 27 to 7.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | August 16th, 2026
text: Oh, sorry about that, coach. Uh first uh first zoom error there. >> It's preseason, buddy. I get it. >> Um just wanted to ask you about the you know the quarterbacks as you go into these games with the quarterbacks, you know, Deion going first and then Shedeur as it was in Chicago and vice versa. Do you script the start of each halves or the start of each of their their sort of their times out to sort of maximize their opportunities there or do you once you get into the flow of the game whether it's third whoever's coming in the third quarter, fourth quarter, do you sort of just kind of let it ride there? >> Well, the opening script we did for Deion and then when we get together at halftime, it's a little bit easier. It's a great question. Uh when we when we're able to go on defense to start the second half, it's easier cuz hell, it's only 13 minutes at halftime to try and all right, what are they doing? What do we want to stay out of? Uh we were getting double cat, so we were trying to fix it on the sideline some of the runs we liked and then what did we want to stay out of? So, we do uh we did this past weekend come up with another script basically what we liked uh for Shedeur but we did have the openers uh for Deion. >> Also, just just one other and this isn't a quarterback related but uh Amani Marshall uh was the the third running back up. Has he sort of surpassed Raheem in the pecking order there or was there something specific you wanted to see out of Amani there? >> I wouldn't say that. I would see them as an or. You know, I would expect to see Rocket going first as the third back this week. I think they're both competing for that third running back spot. >> All right, next we'll go to Scott. >> Hey Todd. Um when you look back on the film, um did the you see anything different about your quarterback evaluation back and watch it? >> Um No, other than there was as I said a number of times where just the quarterbacks being on the road in and out of the huddle using silent cadence that that was apparent that we still have work to do. Now the next two weeks will be at home normal cadence, we'll get to practice with the Bills, still a work in progress, but that was that was probably the most frustrating thing was we spent so much time getting in and out of the huddle, getting our subs were good. Like that part was good. I thought our communication from the sideline on the field that that I got frustrated the other day was good. We didn't we didn't have issues with for the most part, we had 11 on the field, broke the huddle. We just got to continue to work to not waste plays. We took a delay of game, took a timeout missed had a missed cadence on the fumble snap by Shador and there were a couple others that formationally again, just getting used to again, being on the road. That's why we're doing it. Us as a coaching staff and then us as players. So that that was probably the the biggest thing just a reminder of of those, but everything else was pretty much what I saw down there, what I thought. So So from there there wasn't like anything where I thought, well we got a little push here, we got this here. Pretty much what I thought. >> And I know what you said about splitting reps against the Bills on Thursday. How are you going to handle Monday through Wednesday with the two quarterbacks? >> I was just talking to Jake about that, coach Pat Jake and I think we're going to go Shador Monday and Wednesday and Deion Tuesday, Thursday, but Thursday's really both. >> Yeah. >> So, it's really I'm I meet with Joe Brady here at 4:00, so it's just trying to get blocks set up in each say it's run downs. Can we get 16 plays or maybe we go five with the ones, threes with the twos, five with the ones, threes with the twos, and that means both quarterbacks will get five reps in each block. Uh run downs, pass downs, red zone, uh two-minute. And uh but it was really I think it had to be an eight plays, I think something like that, maybe a little more than that. Uh but I I thought they played fine. I mean, cuz we didn't see all of the Bears ones. So, we're going to have to definitely uh be ready to go on Thursday. >> And then uh the run offense when you watch it back on film, what did you uh what did you determine? we certainly didn't scheme for them. We were trying to get it right on the film. We just didn't. That was a starting point then. There were there was a variety of um reasons why. Some schematically and some we just got to play better. Got to get better movement off the ball and and better backside cut off on certain runs. >> Next we'll go to Fred. >> Yeah coach uh adding on to the offensive line there. Um is it any more settled at center and right guard? You know with the injuries you have is Elton seem like he's kind of settling in at center? >> I think that's where we're at right now with Parker being down. Uh the Elton there and Tevin at right guard. There's still a lot of you know a lot of football here in the next couple weeks getting through really the plan for sure has to be when we get done with New England. Um and I'm not sure that uh with practicing with them on Thursday and then all the way to Saturday but I expect to get a decent amount of guys back this week and hopefully the same amount next week. >> Next we'll go to Cam. >> Todd I wanted to ask about the third phase of the game. You had all three of the punters in that position battle out there in the first preseason game. Andre Smith hitting that 50-yard field goal Like big picture, what are you seeing from your special teams unit so far this summer and after that one preseason game in the books? >> Well, I mean, first of all, we went into it with the punters to see all of them and give them opportunities and like any young players, just like offensively and defensively, it's good to play these preseason games. Whether you're the punters or you're any part of the special teams, it was fun to watch those guys play. We certainly have a lot of work to do. I thought we were pretty good on special teams making the initial um field goal and then our coverage units were pretty good. Punt punt, we kind of outkicked our coverage once, but I thought those guys were good. Um I I thought probably we were the closest to being game ready on special teams. Not that we were perfectly clean, but I did think that uh our guys played at a very high level. >> I had a another question about just that the quarterback competition. Before the game, you said that you know, you were looking forward most to just let letting them go out there and and letting it rip. Like does let it rip have a different definition to you uh in that in that kind of scenario? >> Well, when I'm saying that, I'm saying it really for the players as much as anything to let it rip. I I'm a big believer in it's hurt me at times that I've said it before, like being a perfectionist sometimes can make you indecisive. Like you you want it to be perfect and you're not going to be perfect. You you're just not. You've got to go out there. We've got a 40-second clock, right? By the time we get the call in, you don' don't have 5 minutes to decide what protection you're going to get us into, what play. We're working under the gun, so you've got to live with your decision and shrink the margin for and then you got to let it rip. You got to go. And cuz if you at times trying to be perfect leads to indecision, it will this work? What if they do this? What if they do this? What if they do this? And then you're just paralyzed. That's what I meant by that. More than not not so much in the play calls for Miami, but more along the quarterbacks of it's okay. You're not going to play perfect. I'm not going to call it perfect. There's plenty of things I wish we would have done better. You know, and when we went in the game, another part of it was we weren't trying to move people in positions. Like in a game you're going to tag players to play certain spots, right? Um, whether you're asking them to block or receiver or tight ends and what they do well, we just want to see guys in spots and see how they reacted. >> Uh, yeah, Todd, just wondering when I'm looking over the practice schedule the way that you described it, um, it seems pretty heavy Shador for this week uh, with him going Monday, Wednesday, then half of Thursday, then starting the game on Saturday. I mean, you're not it's not going to be perfect. So, if you're going to alternate it, Wednesday, well, first of all, tomorrow will be in shells, we'll go an hour and 45 minutes. Wednesday we'll go in shorts and get a lot of red zone work. So, really Deshaun going Tuesday in a longer practice will get a a more reps in those days and then they're going to we're going to try to split the reps. So, there wasn't really a concerted effort. This seems like a pretty big week for him, obviously, with getting the start and everything. What are some things that you would really like to see from him this week? >> Well, he's improved so much. I mean, he really has in terms of climbing the pocket, working through his progressions. I think that's a big thing. Even on the one that he threw to you know, to 81 in the slot like he drifted a two-deep. I mean, we we caught him in the blitz, but they weren't even close, created kind of his own pressure. Um so, um there's some things he can And then, operation, you know, it's still a part of it. Getting in the huddle, getting lined up, getting the the the call. So does Deion. They're both in the same manner. Uh so, we can stack plays together. We did a good job. Maybe the most positive thing we did yesterday was we overcame some penalties. For God's sakes, we overcame the first and 25, we overcame a couple other penalties. Uh and we hit that big third and 13. Shedeur did. So, how can we play cleaner at all positions? And certainly with him, how can he play cleaner? >> Next, we'll go to Jeff and then we'll wrap up with Scott. >> Hey Todd, can you just give us an update on the players who were injured >> Oh, shoot. I don't have the list with me. Um What do we got? Peters over here. Peter, I'll get me right. >> Coates and Evans. >> Yeah, Coates. again, I don't know exactly where he's at. And uh Evans, I think is going to be fine. Coates, I think hopefully we'll have him back sometime this week. Felt like he was okay this morning and we'll we'll know a little bit more this afternoon on Bates Brendon Bates. >> All right. >> But we've been pretty lucky knock on wood, you know, through camp. We really haven't lost anybody yet long long term like for the year. We haven't had any major injury. We've had some you know, some little nicks and bruises and different things that keep you out and some some muscle muscle issues, but we're we're fine. >> All right, thank you. >> Next we'll go to Scott. >> Hey Todd, I think you said that you thought Spencer finally looked good for a rookie. What did you like about his performance and where do you think he needs to clean it up? >> Well, he's just got to play. I do think he competes and I said that back when he got in that little scuffle with Jared, you know, a little bit of bite back, little bit of uh competitive fire. I do think that all of the different looks that come up in a game basically post snap. It's one thing to be pre-snap. It's another when the defensive line starts to move and when you're going against a different front like other than walk-throughs and prepping for the Bears, we hadn't gone against the odd front. He'd never seen a unless it rarely has he seen a five technique to his side and a sand backer. So there's certain things that you've got to go through and keep learning and put it in your memory bank, you know, and be able to function and I he's certainly plenty athletic enough, certainly plenty smart enough and he's only going to continue to ascend. When you're wired the right way, you've got a competitive stamina, you're smart, you're athletic. I think he's he's going to definitely continue to ascend. >> Thanks. All right, that'll be it for today. Thanks, coach. >> All right, thanks, guys.

title: Ja'Kobi Lane Speaks to Reporters After Positive Preseason Debut | Baltimore Ravens
text: Playing in that though, I mean, you just played in your first NFL game. How did it feel? What were the emotions like? >> Yeah, I can't thank God enough. It's such a such a blessing and I I'm I I can't stress enough to all the young kids out there that this is nothing but hard work, dedication, and consistency. And I think it's very easy to say that, but when you're in there day in and day out as a young young guy or young young woman, I think it's one thing to really consider how you want to be in in life. And I think it's just you want to be a product of what you put in. I think that that's what I want to be. >> How well you played in the last couple weeks of training camp. Did you feel any pressure? Or something you thought about like, "Okay, I I want to make sure I show it's you know in a real game or preseason game?" >> Yeah, I think relying on my teammates, knowing that we've been all preparing for this moment throughout rookie mini camp to OTAs and training camp. This is just a byproduct of everything we put in. So, there there's no pressure knowing that all the guys around me have just worked as hard. And I'm just just one of one of 11 that that has to do one one of 11th of the job. So, super blessed to be in this position. >> What was your reaction? >> postgame here in the locker room and maybe the message that coach Arthur shared. >> Yeah, definitely just stack on this. Very very grateful to get this, but set the foundation for the season and just try and form an identity and and nothing but that. I think as as good as this is, it is a preseason game and we want to enjoy it, but at the same time stack from this and and get ready for what's next. >> I think everybody that came to the stadium was hoping to see a Jacoby long touchdown. What was your thought process last night as you were thinking about this game? And how did you enter the game? >> Yeah, just just super blessed to be in this position. I've been dreaming of this moment all my life, but I think at the end of the day it's a team sport and I'm just I'm just one of 11th of like like I said before. So, just super grateful to be able to be a part of a group like this and and really take the pressure off me and not really think about what I have to do or trying to go above and beyond to make a play and really know that everybody's going to handle their job. And if I do my job, then it's It's good. >> How were you feeling coming today, first NFL game, just kind of walking in? What are the emotions kind of as you kind of walked out on the field for the first time today? >> Yeah, I definitely see the the the why coach coach Decklin stresses preparation and detail so much cuz I feel like throughout the weeks we've been so detailed on the plays we had in and although it wasn't super crazy plays, I think the the fact that we all studied it so well and we were all so dialed, I think it just goes to show that if you really study the plays and you you go in and you have intention with every play you can go above [clears throat] and beyond. >> Can you quickly take us through that, the 16-yard touchdown? >> Uh yeah, definitely just a in cut, try and press space, come out looking for the ball and and from there just get in the end zone. So, I think I've done it a bunch of times during training camp OTAs and I think that's that just goes to show that it's is no different on game day. >> Did you plan your touchdown celebrations or how that one go? >> Pure emotion. I don't I don't think I planned it. >> Oh, did you thought you were going to chuck the ball or when did you say you know what, nah, not this time? >> Halfway through. >> [laughter] >> Jacoby, you know, a really strong game for, you know, a lot of the rookies including Elijah, including Matthew, Benga. What do you think your rookie class kind of said about yourselves and what you could say in a preseason game today? >> Yeah, I think it just goes to show what what we've been brought into and I think all the the vets have just go gone in and and done a great job of welcoming welcoming us with open arms, excuse me, and being able to just show us what their routine and their daily habits, how to really take it and I think all the rookies have done a great job, not not only the drafted guys, but the undrafted guys, they've done a tremendous job just taking this opportunity for what it is and we've all grown as a group and I'm I'm just super grateful to not only be a part of a rookie class like this, but just a team in general. I think they they've done a great job bringing some great guys into the rooms and we we've been growing a lot, so it's super cool. >> It was a with a camp you've had, the game you had tonight, there's a lot of excitement building around you. How are you handling that? >> Yeah, I think it's it's super fun to to be a part of a a hype train, but at the same time, uh this all can go down by by one drop ball, and I I don't mean to say that uh I'm planning on it happening, but I know very well it can happen, but at that same time, I'm still going to be the same person every day, still still come to work with my guys, and and rely on them just like they rely on me. So, I think being able to have that mindset every day, I'm just super blessed to be able to be in this position and and rely on guys like this. So, yeah.

title: Tucker Kraft reflects on his first day of team drills during training camp
text: How was the dream of you being out there for 11-11s? Had a pretty good day, just did it feel good to get back into team drills kind of at full speed now? >> Yeah, absolutely. It felt good um getting my hands on my teammates, you know, making contact again. Surviving the the ground, um do the catch, and uh just beating. >> How big of a milestone in this timeline is today for you? And are you on kind of a snap count for now? >> Yeah, snap count for sure. Like like I've said since the beginning of training camp, they have a plan for me, and week by week they're going to gradually increase my snap count depending on the full rep range of practice. So, you know, my job is just out there to and uh answer when my number's called. >> Did you put a little extra mustard on that spike in the end zone? >> It was bittersweet, that's for sure. Uh it I mean, my first competitive 11-on-11 been uh touchdown, so just excited. >> You look at what you did today, you looked like yourself out there. The strength for you out there, it looked like everything that we've come to know you as. Did it feel like you were yourself today? >> Yeah, I'm just getting back on the horse. Um hopefully I can not now that I've gotten back to um team reps as I continue to um accumulate reps, I hope I can continue to rise my game as well, you know, um take myself you know, to new heights rather than just return to pre-injury. >> Talk to they tell you like is it a gradual thing where you'll do more or will there be times where maybe do a little less before you do more if if that makes sense? >> Absolutely. If you don't want to return to that level and and better than that, what is better than the best tight end in the league look like? >> Well, I just want to diversify my abilities. Um people think I'm a run routes versus man. They think I'm just a a zone catching you know, tight end get drop step get north after the catch, but you know, I I want to continually prove people wrong about what they think my box of abilities are. You know, I'm I'm been watching a lot of film this offseason, taking bits and pieces from other tight ends game and and just trying to add to my own repertoire and and you know, be be a force on this offense when I'm off the field. It's it's seen. >> Some people have don't say they or whatever on social media any comments of them. It seems like you kind of use it as motivate Is that something you use as motivation for yourself? >> Oh, of course. I mean, um it's kind of silly not to When people say that they they don't necessarily get affected by outside noise, you know, to each their own. I mean, I would say you know, lights a fire under my ass. Throws me throws me into more of a competitive mindset. >> Who are some guys that you've been watching and what have you been picking from their game? >> Um I watched a lot of San Fran this off season. I've just I watched I mean at this point I've I've seen every one of our games about three times over now, so watching um watching a lot of San Fran, you know, same same offensive scheme. Maybe taking pieces of what what George is capable of, yards after catches well, um yards per route ran, what how how is he so successful at those attributes? So just just trying to take bits and pieces from a guy who's who's playing 10 years now. >> It's tough. I ask this from a place of respect. Why are you doing this? Like you're in the last year of contract, you're arguably the best tight end in football. You probably deserve to be paid like it. You're absorbing some risk by being out there in 11-on-11. >> I always put it back on the team. Like every one of these guys comes in here and and we this is a violent sport and we risk life and limb, you know, guys guys have to medically retire. They banging heads. They got messed up necks, backs, you know, how many times can you blow a knee out, you know, guys guys keep fighting and and clawing to come back into this locker room. And that that's the that's the reason I do it, you know, I there's other attributes and I I want to leave a legacy on this sport as a whole. You know, I want I want my my children to see the lengths I would go to to fight for something I love and and I think I I have it right here in the G. >> Brian has made it clear all off season that you are a priority since immediately after last season. Is it too much to read into the fact that you're out there doing 11-on-11? title: B.J. Green II & Jabbar Muhammad Recap Performance vs. Saints | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: I know we got good some good work in there. Pretty much that first half it was delightful. Man, I was just out there imposing my will. I wanted everybody out there to have to account for me at all times. Like I've been saying before, I'm just going out there and playing like me. You know, I'm just having fun with it. You know, it's the first game you get to play somebody else. So, I'm going out there and just cutting it loose. >> Did you think you did well? >> Oh, yeah. I think I could have been way more dominant than what was displayed. But, I made the plays that came to me. Um there's a lot of stuff we can learn from. But, at the end of the day, you know, it was the first time out. I did a lot of good things. Things I can sharpen cuz at the end of the day you're chasing greatness, you're chasing dominance. You know, every time I came to the sideline I would get pointers from Trey Josh. Go out there and correct it, you know, make sure you get pressure. So, yeah. I'm I'm good. It's It's a good stepping stone. But, it's nowhere I'm not satisfied. >> You've had a very good camp. Is it good to see it go in action as well, not just on the practice field? >> Uh I think it's just it's another stepping stone. Like I said, you know, we play each other, you do good against each other. You can play good against somebody else, you can play good against somebody else, but we're not satisfied with good. I'm not satisfied with good on this team. Nobody really is. I think that's what make this team special, you know. You know, obviously the first half was a little bit bumpy, but you know, we we're very resilient as a team. You know, we we know what it looks like to look into the face of adversity and come back out on it. And that says a This says a lot about the people here. So, I mean, you know, it was great, honestly. >> How how far did you jump for that fumble or or dive, I should say? >> I don't know. Everything just stopped. Like I just like It's kind of like a dog. Like squirrel, it's the ball. So, I mean, I'm happy I got it, so. >> How about to see a guy like Muhammad make a play like that, come down to a defensive play to end the football game, and you know that guy's trying to make a make a name for himself? >> I'm not surprised. I'm not surprised at all. I mean, I knew Jabari in college, so he's been like that. I mean, he just Everybody's just now noticing it, so. I've been knew exactly what he was, what he was capable of, how he he can go to the he go toe-to-toe with anybody. If I see anybody brings Jabrill, I'm going to pick Jabrill 10 out of 10 times. So, everybody else is excited all that. I'm like, it's a reg- it's a regular occurrence. It's still, you know, all props to him and, you know, being able to shut out the game, but, you know, that's those those are the things that you expect from guys who step up to the plate like that day to day. >> Thanks, man. Thank you. Appreciate it. >> And then, talk to me about the reaction you're getting right now. >> Uh it's good. I mean, at the end of the day, these guys are somebody who I go to war with every day. Obviously, we're in training camp right now, so um just being around those guys, seeing them happy for me right now is a good feeling. >> How do you think you did coming into this game and then the results that you were getting? [clears throat] >> Yeah, I mean, I can always be better, for sure. I feel like a lot of them tip-for-tat plays, I got to end up finishing those. Um and that's how I felt throughout the week, really, but at the end of the day, man, it's not how you start, but how you finish. And going out there to make the game still in play, it feels real good. >> I mean, you were my player to watch. I'm going to humble brag about that. You went out there, you did what you needed to do, you got the pass breakups, you got the ball stopped, you stopped the players on the same side. How good does it feel to have that under your belt and now go into the next week of training camp, the next preseason game, and just improve from there? >> I mean, it's a grind, but right now, like I said, it feels really good. We're going to soak this one in. Obviously, got to watch the film, there's a lot to improve on, like coach just said, but it feels great. Uh at the end of the day, like I said though, there's a lot to improve on, but right now it feels pretty good. >> What do you take away from this game? >> Um we just got to communicate better. Uh go watch the film um at the end of the day. Keep improving, but uh right now we're going to live in the moment and try to uh get back to the drawing board. >> Nice. Keep going. >> Are you guys good? >> Mhm. >> Jumping in. I don't know where I'm jumping in. Just got done with coach, but uh how about the ups and downs for you in the game? I mean, really, to the last play. Just played a lot of ball and, you know, it's nature of your position, right? How quickly do you have to forget? >> That's the life of a corner. Uh but at the end of the day, going against uh the guys I go against in practice every day kind of, you know, shapes you for this moment. Uh those guys are really, really good. And you know, you come out here, you you don't flinch really. Uh next play mindset and I feel like that's what we did today. >> How important for you to make plays in this setting because it seems like you've been making plays in the practice setting so much? >> It was it's important. Obviously, you know, you want to translate it to the to the game field under the big lights. Um like I said earlier, uh a lot of those tip-for-tat plays I do want to make and I'm going to work on that for sure. But, um just being able to finish that like we did, um it was pretty surreal. >> Does your confidence take a jump in in a big moment like that to make that kind of play? >> Um and my confidence stays high, especially at corner. You you you can't derail, never, cuz then you start doing stuff that you don't usually do. Uh confidence is the number one thing at cornerback. Uh nickel corner, whatever whatever the case may be. You're on an island all day against their fastest players going backwards. So, you got to have that confidence in your technique and your job and things like that and trust your teammates. But, my confidence never took a shape. >> You probably didn't know this, but coach was trying to call a timeout before that last play, didn't get it. >> I'm glad I'm glad he I'm glad it didn't happen. Shoot, I'm glad it didn't happen. >> One last one for you. You've done up to this point probably a a lot of what you can do. How important are the next 2 weeks for you to continue to stack and and I guess not let let go of some of that momentum you've built? >> I mean, at the end of the day, I just take it day by day. Um obviously, you know, you want to come out here and show the coaches that you can improve. You want to show the coaches that you know the playbook, uh your versatility, even on special teams and things like that. But, um I'm never going to waver. I'm never going to go up or down. I'm stay even-keeled and try to do what I do every single day.
