That's That's things that we stress offensively. And you know, as as you put more and more film on tape, you know, you you get more and more predictable. So, you got to keep finding ways to evolve, but you know, that's as a coach, I'd rather be much more, you know, about the basics and being great at the fundamentals. So, that's what we're going to harp on. >> Why is the fullback position important to you? >> Uh well, running the ball is important, you know. We think that's a huge part of of winning football games, you know, running the ball, stopping the run on defense. Uh just in our scheme, you know, it's a very versatile player. Guy that plays tight end, plays fullback, that can that can pass pro, that has to be a four-core special teams player. Uh I think he's got to be one of the smartest players on your team. So, uh we're going to keep getting Connor and uh you know, get him better. And Girdge is coming along. >> To follow along that, what kind of tone from a guy's standpoint can a fullback help set in the running game? >> They can help it, but it's up to them. Yeah. >> Charles Graham is a young man that's really prospered under Rick Dennison. Would you just talk about his maturation under Rick, please? >> Yeah, I would say that you know, I'd say that Charles is is working his tail off, you know, Rick and Mario and Ben and and Coach Pete, you know, that's their job to get those guys better. Charles knows that he has to take another step in his career and he's he's been about the work. He just got to keep keep improving like all these young guys. >> What are your conversations with Jamard after the first game to keep his confidence? >> Uh after the game, none. You know, I talked to him before the game. You know, you know, I they keep that between him and I, but I know I told you guys after the game how proud I was of of all the adversity that he's been through. You know, he you see him out here, he has not missed a practice other than the ones we've kept him out of. Um so, so he's he's just going to keep improving. >> It seems like Malik and Fernando's chemistry continues to grow day by day. How promising or exciting is that to have two rookies coming in like that being able to grow? >> Yeah, time on task, you know, helps everybody get better. So, that that's got to keep getting better. You know, Malik is he's jumped in there with the ones at times as well and he's earned those reps, but you know, he's got to stay humble and stay hungry. >> What did you make of the run defense against Arizona? >> Yeah, obviously overall wasn't the way we wanted it. We got to improve. >> Spencer Burford said that his familiarity with the blocking scheme made him feel more comfortable and he was also able to give input to other guys in the line. Have you seen that and how has that benefited him do you think? >> I have seen that and that was the expectation for Spencer. He's a guy that's played a lot of football that we're counting on to, you know, have a physical season for us. >> Got it. >> Next question. >> Thank you. >> All right. >> Deommodore, a lot of players and coaches have been talking about the defense. >> This year just what do you like about that overall to be in that kind of scheme? >> I think it really plays to my strengths, you know, as a taller, longer corner. Um, you know, being up and being able to make a receiver uncomfortable is something obviously that really plays into my type of game that I like to play. So, I'm really looking forward to that opportunity. >> And what was like going back to your rookie year, what you feel like was the biggest area of improvement that you needed to make and how has the whole time you've focused on that and also >> I think the biggest thing for me was just getting the experience of being out there on an NFL field. Um, you know, we're still learning the position and you know, it didn't always have the confidence I needed to succeed and you know, had a couple of rough weeks, but really tried to dive into everything, all the fundamentals that make great corners great. Footwork, press work, things like that. Coming into this season, just keep improving. >> How do you feel like you built up that >> How you said how? confidence going into this season? >> Uh, like I said, kind of really like the experience, you know, like um, you know, guarding NFL guys, professionals week in and week out, you know, over time has just helped build my confidence. When you make a couple plays, you know, the confidence just keeps stacking and I feel like throughout camp um, I've made plays and uh, coaches have put me in position to do that, so um, the confidence just keeps building from there. >> Several of your teammates have talked about the coaching. Just there's so much of it, it's so detailed. And for a guy like you that's high football IQ, it seems like this is a perfect environment for you. Are you seeing that like your teammates? >> Absolutely. Um, you know, the detail is so important in this defense and the coaches harp on that, but you know, for people for us players, you know, it take it's a lot of accountability on our part to really hone in and dive into the detail, so you can be in the right spot to make a play. Not just knowing what you're doing, but what everyone else is doing and that's going to put you in position to make the >> You talked about the accountability factor and obviously in the game >> the other day that there was about 16 straight completions by the opposing offense. You guys going to take that personally when you you come into this week? >> Absolutely. Um, you know, as a secondary, we we never want to put that on our resume, but you know, it happens, so now we just have to learn from it and we have obviously um, and just try to, you know, put that to rest and not let that happen again. >> Was there an emphasis on, you know, the make the intensity or the physicality in practice that this week since then? >> No, making plays is a mindset, you know, you know, breaking up a pass, making an interception, it's a mindset. And yeah, it comes down to your detail and your discipline, but when the ball isn't there, you got to go get it. So, that's as a collective the mindset that we have. So. >> Joe Woods is still your position coach and Rob Leonard just switched roles, but how how different is maybe what you're being asked to do this year from last year or how similar? >> I think in terms of what we're doing, it's a little different, so obviously there was a learning curve there, just learning, you know, obviously with a new DC, there's going to be some new things schematically, but, you know, as a cornerback, your role is pretty simple. Don't let them catch the ball. So, um that pretty much stays the same. Obviously, comes in different ways, but um the overall rule is pretty much the same. But, for me, personally, you know, having a year under my belt, and we got a lot of young DBs in the room, trying to be a leader and a resource to them, just to make them better and feel more comfortable and help them in any way that I can. >> Talk about that young DBs room. And obviously, you're still young yourself as really competitive. How do you manage to find that, you know, a balance between having to compete against these guys for a job, but also like helping them out along the way as a teammate? >> I mean, the competition comes down who's going to be the best, and I want the best guy out there. And if it's me, that's great. If it's not me, you know, obviously, I'm going to keep competing to make it that way, but you're only as strong as your weakest link. So, you got to bring everyone along with you in that room, cuz we're going to need all of them. >> This is your first NFL off season after I mean, after you your first season. Um What did you How did you change up your um your preparation this off season to to go into your second year? >> Well, I think now just learn knowing what to expect. I mean, obviously, you're going to train throughout the off season, which I have, but now it's not so much of a surprise. You know, you know what you're getting into, so a lot of emphasis on footwork, but not doing too much to where you're going to hurt yourself, you know, being smart about it, but um like I said, just knowing what you're going to get out of a full long season um really helps with the preparation. >> How much of your off season did you spend scouting, looking back at your first season, and trying to, you know, maybe learn from maybe your tape, that kind of thing? >> A lot. You know, um I wasn't always happy I was not happy with how I played uh all the time last year, and there were times where I knew I had to be better, and I knew I could be better, so it was a lot of reflecting for me on what my weaknesses were, and really trying to dive into that throughout OTAs, throughout mandatory mini camp, and now throughout training camp. You know, it was a lot of self-reflecting, a lot of self-scouting, honestly. >> Can you at times be your own worst critic? >> Absolutely. That's No one's going to be harder on me than I I'm going to be on myself. And you know, it's it's walking a fine line between Yeah, obviously you have to keep pushing yourself, but it gets to the point where you feel like you're never satisfied even yourself, no matter what. So, I've had to learn to balance that, but I will always No, like I said, no one's going to be harder on me than I am on myself, cuz I want to be perfect. I'm a perfectionist, and you play an imperfect game in an imperfect position. So, it's it's a balance, for sure. >> Terrence is a veteran addition to the secondary. What has he brought to to this unit, and do you feel like he's kind of underrated with all that he can do back there? >> Absolutely. Terrence has been a great Obviously, he's played a lot of football. He's been a great veteran for me and for this room just with his his versatility, you know, his knowledge of the game, his leadership. You know, you feel you feel that as soon as he steps in the building, as soon as he steps in our room. And the first day I knew he was going to be a great asset for us. >> All right. Thank you. >> I texted your brother a pretty funny picture of you. >> He responded or not? Did he respond? >> Camp for you, you're so versatile. You play right You can play running back, tight end. You you can fullback, obviously special teams. Would you talk about your versatility in Clint's system? >> Yeah, I feel like all the me and Pat, just not myself, we're versatile, but everybody on the offense side, you have to be able to play multiple positions, be able to block, whether you're receiver You guys obviously saw Jack doing that a lot, but we have a lot of capable receivers and a lot of versatile guys on offense. You know, and I'm just trying to do my 111, so um guys might view it as that, but I just view it as doing my job. >> Uh Connor, what's just your overall impressions of like like that running back duo you guys have between Ashton and Jalen and Mike Washington? >> Yeah, it it's unbelievable. Uh obviously, uh you guys saw what Ashton's done in college uh and what he did last year as a rookie. And uh just being, you know, right next to him every day, um you know, he wows me every day. And then Mike coming here, um bigger back, but you see the explosion, you know, you see both their vision. Um you know, and I'll be able and I think they'll both be able to compliment each other, but uh you know, Ashton's a great leader and uh you know, obviously, he's the guy in the room, but you know, we have so many guys in there that are going to push him and you know, make make us all overall better. >> You can talk about versatility, but when it comes to having that full back position on the field, how unpredictable does it make the offense cuz there's so many things that you can do? >> Yeah, you can, you know, throw the ball, run the ball, um you know, stretch the stretch the defense uh horizontally and vertically. Um but that's a coach, you know, and his scheme. Uh it's just not myself. Uh it's just uh the scheme and, you know, and buying in honestly and you know, you guys saw that on the first drive and you know, you guys saw that glimpse throughout the game, but we just got to ultimately put it together. Um and you know, it's not the finished product right now. Um you know, and we don't want it to be. We just want to continue to get better. Um and this camp's about growth and this season's about growth. >> Just what's it been like with you and Payton Thorne? >> Uh great. Uh obviously, looked up to him uh going to Michigan State. Um and you know, being next to him is, you know, as well. Uh he's a a great leader. Uh somebody that can command the offense and you know, when you're in the huddle with him, it it's just very calming and uh when you're in there with a vet quarterback like that, it helps everybody else and uh he can talk to all the guys and you know, make sure everybody's hearing the message. Uh you know, and he's fully bought in and um you know, he's helping Fernando as well. >> All right, well talk about that. What what has stood out to you about like Fernando and the way he competed more adjusted to playing at Colorado? >> Yeah, uh he's impressed me every day just um with the the mental process honestly just uh how much he puts into it and obviously you guys saw uh this past weekend and you know, you're going to get what you put in. Um and he's dialed in and he's about the team um and he wants to earn everything um which is that much more special. Uh I've been around rookie quarterbacks and you know, younger quarterbacks but um he's at the top of the list honestly. >> Do you feel like that the mental mental preparation which is fair as overall? You find it kind of rare to see from a from a young guy like that? >> Yeah, for sure. Uh at a quarterback position you have to prepare uh you know, more different than uh anybody else and probably more than anybody else but um he he's taken that on and he's done that every day and he's done it even more. You see him here early mornings, late night walking through the the indoor by himself uh with one of the other rookie quarterbacks going through the script script just you know, bringing other guys along and uh when you have a quarterback like that, you know, it the future's very bright. >> Do you see some Le'Veon Bell in Mike Washington to speed, the power, the ability to just kind of move guys around? >> Yeah, uh you know, I I see I see that uh in his game but also see just Mike Washington. Um a bigger back with you know, speed. I don't think Le'Veon was running 4-3. Um and you know, that's nothing against Le'Veon but you know, Le'Veon was more uh 4-5 4-6 ish you know, kind of hesitate but Mike can hit it too. Um but he has that in his game. Um and you know, I think I think he'll just continue to uh reveal himself and you know, just be himself and that's what I can can continue to tell him like you're going to mess up. You know, I mess up and then as year five it's going to be okay um and just take it one rep at a time. >> How would you describe the mentality required to play the fullback position? >> Uh just being selfless uh and doing your 111. Uh you know, you might get the ball here and there but you know, that's not what it's about. It's about uh you know, opening up lanes and you know, getting the run game going and you know, having the run game marry up with the pass game and just honestly doing the dirty work and uh you know, special teams as well. So uh it's a full day's work and you know, it's never going to stop. >> John, at your career did you settle into the fullback position and mentality? >> Uh this past year, honestly. I I feel like I've always had the mentality, but uh in my first four years in the NFL I was playing true Y and true F, so sometimes I was in line. Um but I feel like this fits more of my skill set, but uh you know, Patrick's a great fullback as well and we're just trying to get better each day. Uh and uh coach P as well has worked with us and really trying to hone in on our uh our craft and uh our pad level and continue to, you know, run our feet cuz it's more than, you know, just running and, you know, trying to create a hole and just run at, you know, somebody and, you know, like a brick wall. Uh it's, you know, caving a hole and you know, sometimes there's not a hole and, you know, you're just going to hit color and the play sometimes messed up, but just uh you know, playing through the whistle and that's something that I'm trying to improve on as well. >> It's kind of following that system that values the fullback position. What were those conversations like about you coming on board and now that you're here, you know, what does it mean to kind of see the way that the fullback has been used here under coach Kubiak? >> Yeah, uh when coach reached out to me, I knew the opportunity and it was an opportunity that I couldn't pass up and, you know, I'm glad I'm here. Everybody's embraced me, the coaches, players and, you know, I just am continuing to get acclimated each and every day, but you know, that's just, you know, credit to everybody else around here. >> On the back end of that, I guess how different is the way that Clint Kubiak views the fullback and how he used it versus any other system that you've been in so far? >> Yeah, it's completely different. Uh just have even having coach Kubiak as the offensive head coach that's something new for me. Uh you know, he's very, you know, big on his details and um I've always had a head coach that's, you know, a defensive head coach and uh he he's going to, you know, push myself, but everybody else to get better. Um doesn't matter. He's going to find the flaw in the play and, you know, you want to coach like that. >> For a guy that does so much, how much do you like his creativity? >> Yeah, uh I'm continuing to see that, uh um so far I've seen, you know a little bit of it and I'm sure he's not going to show too much in the preseason, but coach Kubiak has a lot of you know bags of tricks you know up his sleeve and you guys saw that in Seattle, you know with all the guys they had, you know, you Warner, you had the returner that they got from the Saints late. Um JSN obviously, Cooper Kupp, but you know, here we have a lot of guys as well. You got Trey Tucker, Jaylen Nailor, Jack Besh, Brock Bowers obviously, Michael Mayer, Ashton Jeanty, Mike Washington, Dillon Lobby. There's a there's a bunch of capable guys and it's just everybody you know buying in and doing their job and I think we have a a team that's very team oriented and you know, that's going to get you out of dark times when you need it. >> What's the biggest step that the offense wants to take from the first preseason season game to Houston? >> Uh just being consistent. Uh first drive went well, um highs and lows, you know, throughout the second, third, and fourth, but just putting each drive together and uh you know, there was so many little details that we left on the field even myself, um you know, that we all learned from and we're going to go to Houston and have a great couple days of practice and then be able to show that and put that on tape this week. >> A lot is made of the zone rushing scheme and this kind of Shanahan's tree play Kubiak offense, but we also saw a lot of gap scheme in the first game. Can you talk about how like balanced this rushing attack is between kind of finesse running and power running? we obviously got to stay balanced. There's a lot of great defenses out there, so you can't just go out there and just run you know counter and power run the whole game, but we're wide zone team and when you put stress on you know the corners and you know make them tackle like that, we have very capable backs and it's really just about you know, putting our backs on you know, the corners and safeties and even linebackers whether that's just running routes out the backfield cuz they're just so versatile, so we can mix and match up you know, so many guys on our offense, so it'll be interesting to see. >> Thanks, Connor. >> Thank you guys. I appreciate it. Thank you.

title: Colts players on rookie impact, position rotations
text: George, what what uh what lessons did you kind of get after watching the the tape the other night? >> Uh from the game? >> Yeah, from the game. Sorry. Yeah. >> Uh shoot. One thing I probably learned just like just just working on um some more that just beating the chipper, you know, just that's one [snorts] thing I learned by myself. I need to definitely work on just beating the chipper just just to be a little bit more effective in that in that part. Like, okay, I'm getting chipped now. I got to be also effective in the rushes. It's like you don't want to just get say I got chipped and that's the end of your rush, >> right? Uh we also we always hear about the speed of the game being different, you know, from college to the NFL. I know it's preseason, but did you notice that and did you feel like you adjusted well to it? >> Uh I really I feel like it was like regular speed for me. I feel like I feel like the SEC pretty much got me uh prepared for uh the NFL. Like the speed is pretty much the similar. The size and speed is pretty much the same to me. >> Your team so far, you know, what sticks out for you? Uh something probably sticks out for me like just like my ability to like just get in the playbook and just like you know just just be detail or oriented with the plays and just like staying focused like on that just like main just taking it day by day and just like stay in my playbook. So like know when I get my chances out there I don't go out there and bust like that's my my biggest focus right now. >> You're here to be a pass rusher obviously big picture but when it comes like special teams how do you find yourself really sinking into that a little bit? I I definitely feel like I'm I'm getting more comfortable in it. I'm take taking my time day by day with it. You know, just I know that's going to be a big part of my career, especially now since I'm a rookie. Um you know, just I just got to take special teams and like shoot take it how I approach everything else. You know, I I brand myself as a high effort player that played violin. I just feel like if I could just bring that to special team, it'll be good. >> What's uh what's been the thing that's I guess pleasantly surprised you play so far? Uh, I'll probably say just like um just me being me, like I said, just still being a violent, high effort player, you know, I I still feel like I go out there and fit up blocks even at the NFL level. So, I kind of feel good about that. >> Who did you work with anybody between the end of uh offseason and and now on pass stuff this this summer? >> Uh, yeah, I worked with Dez Pass trainer and Chuck Smith up down in Atlanta for a little bit. So, I feel like they they definitely hone a couple of my skills. Is that is that who you've always worked with or is that new? >> Uh that's pretty new cuz like uh I pretty much just stayed at my school for most of the time through the offseason just to work on my school and do my own thing. >> What was Chuck's message to you about >> uh as a pass? >> Pretty much he just like told me like just shoot work on the smaller things get off important you know like the the core things to pass rush get off you know being and just defining your moves like you know it's like you when you when you get your chance you got to do it once you see you got your one-on-one rush you got to take your chance and win. Have you have you learned some some new I don't know technique-wise. Have you have you learned some things out here or trying to develop some new techniques or anything like that or >> I feel like more my more so my thing is just like just taking what like what what I like to do and then just critiquing it to the point like where it get better. I wouldn't say like I learned something brand new cuz like you know football it's it's not you know once you start playing football for a while it's not so much you you know like know we do the same move since the 1900 1980s you know same cross shot same stab club you know it's just like just like getting better with your hand placement where I want my hand to be what what what I'm keying what I'm keying to his arm I'm trying to get his wrist or his elbow I'm trying to get to the shoulder pad just just being more detail oriented when it comes to that aspect >> those details matter a lot more out here than they do in college I imagine >> no doubt like watching like watching college. Yes, it be one possession, but like here it's like you'll probably say like in your season of college it be like 12 plays that be like make or break your season. I I feel like it's way more in NFL like you know it'll be the margin error is so small here like you know it just be like one small detail just because you didn't smother the shoulder on the flat route and he got a first down when you supposed to that that could be the game right there. They got a first down they going to take a knee you know just something small as that. Yeah. So, you just got to be very detail or detail oriented when you pretty much doing everything in the league. >> Going from training camp into joint practices and everything, is there anything you took from just going against your own team for a couple weeks, going against the Patriots that you want to apply now to Atlanta this week? >> Uh, I'll probably say just, you know, just just keeping um keeping keeping things simple for me. Just like don't don't get like too big on this, that, and the third. Just like keeping things simple like so I can just play fast. Like I'm here to play fast, you know? I'm young. So they want me they want us to be play fast and aggressive. So just keep doing that. >> All right. Thanks. >> Thank you. >> Linebacker room. I mean you know you guys have a lot of competition going on. Guys um kind of switching out for a lot of first team reps the last couple weeks of camp. What what uh is special about this group you guys have? >> Uh you know I just think they did a great job up front of bringing in guys that are ready ready to compete. Um, we've had competition throughout the years of me being here, but you know, this one's different because we got a lot of young guys that are hungry and who have uh the skill sets to to play right now. And so, you know, we push each other a lot in that linebacker room. It's great competition. Like, we we're each other the biggest cheerleaders. Like, we want to see each other do successful things. And, you know, it's a great room. And Iron Shoppers, Iron, that's our our mentality. And, yeah, I mean, we come every day knowing that we got to compete because the next guy behind us is trying to take our job. What's going to surprise people about the Colts defense this year? >> Uh, I think, you know, it's not surprising to us, but it may be surprising to others is the level of physicality that we that we're going to come and bring. And, you know, for us, that's the non-negotiable. That's one of the the pillars of our defense is being uh physical. And, you know, we had spurts last year of it. Uh, but as as a whole, as a whole defense, that's our identity. You know, it starts with that. And as a linebackers, that's where we hang our hats on is the ability to be physical and assert our dominance to the other team. You've seen a lot of new faces walk through the door and now it's all, you know, acclimating. How do you think it's all fitting together? >> I think it's fitting together well. I think, you know, we got a lot, like I said earlier, a lot of people that are hungry for opportunity, a lot of good football players who know how to play the game, who are really coachable, um, who want to compete, and it makes it challenging because like I said, you can't really have a bad day cuz everybody's hunting and everybody is looking for their chance to to move up on the depth chart. And that's how it's got to be. that's that's what's going to allow us to put the the best uh competitive advantage forward for our for the fans, for the organization, and for the team. >> You mentioned the the young guys in that linebacker room. Um CJ Island, who I know has missed some some practice with his injuries, goes back to the day, him and Bryce Ber, what particularly stands out about those two guys that has really impressed me so far. >> I mean, they're they're both uh good in different ways. Bryce is just a he's a natural football player. I mean, he's super physical. He loves the game. He loves running around. He brings juice and energy every day. I sit next to him in meetings and you know he's over there just like I read his notes sometimes and sometimes they make me laugh cuz he's just he's just young and hungry and CJ you know he's great in his own in his own right he has a little bit of old soul more uh you know laidback but when it's time to go like he goes and you know them two they really feed off each other and then on top of that I mean West weeks and and Taj you know those are guys that are are good too and they can play for us too Devin as well so you know it's a deep room and uh I I love to see where where everybody stacks up. >> What what's it do for your confidence that you know a lot of defenses have two three starters and it's kind of static but with Lou and and coach Peter there could be like four or five of you that play a ton of snaps this year. >> Yeah. I mean confidence I think is the most important thing for any position um you got to have self-belief because if you don't you know the game is too hard to for you to be doubting yourself. If you don't believe in yourself then you know you're not giving yourself the best advantage possible. So for me that confidence is um like I said non-negotiable like it it needs to be there no matter where where we are but at the same time when you getting first team reps and when you uh you know you're getting coached hard but you know there's high expectations and it's um you know it makes you feel good and it does give me confidence. So you know Lou coach Lou and coach B have been doing a good job of of instilling that in me and you know I got to keep taking steps forward and become the player that I know I can be. How's uh how's the competition on the back end shaping up just generally right now? >> Um it's going great, man. We got a lot of guys uh a lot of guys can make plays. A lot of people can play. Um and honestly, it brings out the best in you every day just because um you really want to put your best foot forward every day, you know what I mean? Just everybody's pushing everyone, you know, but at the same time, we hold everybody accountable. Um we we've just kind of started something where we just like have our accountability board. if you, you know, you mess up with something in practice, um, it's just something where, you know, nobody's sensitive. It's just, you know, it means more coming from the players, you know what I mean, than, um, the coaches all the time. So, >> you guys point out the mistakes you're saying. >> Oh, yeah. I mean, the coaches obviously going to have their, you know, culture points, but um, we see it on film. You know, it's like jokingly, but it's all love at the same time. But, um, you know, just everybody wants everybody to play their best. So, >> So, what happens when you make the board? >> What happens? >> What happens if you make the board? What happens is there punishment? you know, this is like an internal thing. You know what I'm saying? I can't give out y'all all the juice, but uh it's just like a little competition within all of us. You know what I mean? But at the same time, >> like it means more, like I said, coming from your peers than all the time you just hearing it from the coaches. So, I just feel like it makes everybody better. >> Really broad question, but I mean, what do you think your role specifically is, you know, in all of this? >> I feel like, man, I'm I'm coming in bringing a different energy um just than I guess what they had last year. You know what I'm saying? I'm a different person, you know, than whoever they had. Um, and I've just I have a lot of experience, you know, this is my ninth year and I've been a bunch of different places. So, I'm giving a different perspective to the coaches, uh, the players, like players that have only been here, you know what I mean? And, um, special teams as well. I'm I'm a dog on special teams. So, um, whatever the coaches ask me to do, man, more you could do. That's pretty much been my career. title: Colts and Pacers Sports and Entertainment donate 250K for flood relief
text: Well, thank you guys for being here. I think we want to start by saying our hearts go out to all of our fellow Hoosiers um who have been impacted by the devastating floods this week. Um I think as devastating as these moments are for our state, I'm always really inspired and reminded of the beauty of people coming together. Um, I think that whether it's giving resources or donating your time or donating funds, I think people have already started to do that. Um, and this is actually um, give back Sunday here at Colts Camp. So, we wanted to collectively make an announcement that we are donating $250,000 to Red Cross. Um, and we really want to use this as an opportunity to encourage others to give what they can. Um, small or big or um, any donation of any kind. and there's so many needs. We encourage all fans to please visit redcross.org. Um, see the things that they need, see the ways that you can help. Um, as we all sadly know with, you know, devastation like this right now, um, it's really top of mind, but it's going to take months on end to recover from this. And so, we just encourage people to keep this in mind, keep, um, your fellow Hoosiers and neighbors and community in mind, and come together like Indiana does so, so well. um in times of need. And we also know the financial burden is extreme, but the mental burden that this can take on families and people um are extremely difficult. So, we encourage those as well if they need resources in that space to please visit kickingstigma.org and look at our resource page um for anything there. Um but we I'm going to turn it over, my pleasure to turn it over to Rachel Simon um with the Pacers Foundation to say a little bit more as well. >> Thank you, Kayn. Yeah, I'm I'm also going to repeat that our our hearts and our love go out to all the families affected when this community is in need. I think it's beautiful that we're proud and able to join forces with with the Colts and the ERS family um to help them. This is one community, one neighborhood, and we're here. We're here for each other. I want to thank all the first responders, the Red Cross, everybody that's been on the front line. And as Kayn said, a reminder, and hopefully this this will remind everybody else that there's small things you can do, whether it's volunteering, giving money, and um you know, be there for for our neighbors. So, thank you so much. I'm going to turn it over to >> Terry. >> Terry, thank you. >> Yes. Thank you so much. So, first of all, um my name is Terry Stgden. I'm the CEO for the Indiana region of the American Red Cross. And first and foremost, I want to thank the Indianapolis Colts and Patri Sports Entertainment for this extremely generous gift. Um, the American Red Cross was here before the storms hit. We are here now and we will be here for the months to come to help people recover. At this time, we have 13 shel shelters open. Some are Red Cross run. Some of them are run by our partners and supported by the Red Cross. We have served over 200 people overnight last night in shelters and have fed over 4,700 meals and snacks. Um we are grateful for um everyone's um support uh whether that is you want to step up and volunteer which you can do that at redcross.org/vunteer um or if you want to donate um to help uh fund our efforts which you can be found at redcross.org. If you are in an area that has been impacted and you don't know where to get help, you can call 1800 redcross. If you need shelter or if you have shelter and you just need meals and you need someone to talk to, you can find out where a shelter is close to you at redcross.org/ org/shelter and it will show you all the shelters that are here in in the state of Indiana. Um again, I am grateful for this gen generous gift. It will help us to continue um to serve people here that have impacted and this is a great opportunity for that who's your hospitality to show up not only here in Indiana where we know it is but to make an example to the rest of the world. So, uh thank you very much for this time and thank you for the gift. you grew up in this community. So I mean this is particularly close for you I suppose >> because of that. >> Yes. Um I was you know we were talking beforehand and it is it's emotional to see some of the pictures and videos you know of places I went as a kid. Um or I just in fact was you know a couple weeks ago I was at Connor Prairie. Today I was over by you know Keystone Mall even and seeing you can't even drive on those roads and seeing that it's in fact still slloshing in too. Um and you know have friends who live in all areas that have been affected. Um and so I think it is a very personal thing and you know we talked about it with our kids you know waking up today and and getting in our car just being thankful that we're okay and our homes that are okay. But this is one of those things where reminding people that, you know, just cuz you weren't affected or touched by it to to please, you know, reach out. And I think that I've seen that in so many different ways, you know, from the animal shelters and people, you know, rescuing all of them and moving them into I think every single one was fostered in Muny, for example. um just seeing that kind of hospitality, it's not surprising to me in the state um having grown up here and and really it's one of my favorite things about living and working here um is that and so I know that um everyone will continue to support each other in that way. But yeah, it's definitely difficult to see. >> What was important for you two as Pacers folks to collaborate time before it feels like to do this again at this? >> Yeah, I mean I can do it too, but you go first. Go ahead. I was just gonna say I love I it makes me smile because so often it's either them calling us or us calling them and I don't know if there's ever been a time where either one of us has said no. Um I think that we tend to really want to piggyback off each other and really make that impact that much greater. And so I'm so thankful for our partnership that we have for all these years. >> Absolutely. It's it's incredible to have a partner that you can call and that's going to say yes because they care the family and and the organization just as much about the people here. So, um we're thankful for the partnership thanks to you >> and I think it's unique. >> I think it is unique. I think that we've been told that many times that our relationship is very unique. >> Um and so I think it's a good thing for the state of Indiana. Absolutely.

title: Colts' offense has sloppy day versus the defense
text: Another day of Colts training camp is in the books here at Grand Park. We head next week to pair of joint practices before another preseason game gets underway. But a very active, um, very hot day of action here at Grand Park, uh, for the Colts. I'm Nathan Brown, Colts Insider with the Indianapolis Star. He's Joel A. Erickson. Let's break down what happened on the field today for the Colts. Um, as as strong as this offense has looked throughout, I would say most of training camp, um, across the board, first team, um, sometimes second, sometimes third, um, really struggled today against the Colts defense. Some great play execution by the defense, but honestly some, um, miscues, underthrows, sloppy mistakes from the offense. What what really stood out to you most? >> Yeah, just kind of a thorough whipping uh, by the defense today. Uh, Kwity Paye had a couple of nice rushes. One of them led to a sack. One of them led to a batted ball that turned into a Micah Blackburn interception. Um, but there's also some other stuff, too. Laquon Treadwell, for instance, they get a free play, one of their few gifts the defense gives them. Uh, Jones puts a nice ball out there for him. He's two steps in front of him. He can't make the catch. Couple plays later they throw a pick. It it it it just was one of those days where the offense just they just didn't have it. Like it started with the Jonathan Taylor drop. Um, just my notebook is just carnage, just offensive carnage everywhere. >> Yeah, and it was, uh, and we saw some like some hustle drives, some stuff in the red zone, some normal traditional 11-on-11 work. And it's like across the board there wasn't really, I would say one thing where the offense executed consistently on well today at practice. >> Only Riley Leonard. Riley Leonard looked good in his couple of in his two periods. Um, he I think had the only scoring drive in a move the ball period. Um, they they did one of the sudden change situations. This is as long as we're mentioning all the quarterbacks. With Anthony Richardson and they went tackle for loss, sack, uh, gain of none. And that was the end of that. So it just just a very bad day for for offense. Defense clearly won today. My one big play was the second interception that Daniel Jones threw. Uh tried to go deep to Treadwell who again struggled a little bit today and Cam Bynum came ranging over for what was an underthrown ball and and picked it off. I think one of the things with Treadwell though, and I was thinking about this, if that's Alec Pierce down there, he finds a way to get his hands on that football. And Treadwell really wasn't involved in the catch point of it at all. It's another like you there's a lot of times out here where you're going, man, Alec Pierce in that situation. But that was one where like I said, Alec Pierce has a tendency to get his hands on that even if he doesn't catch it. >> Alec Pierce was out on the field again today not in cleats um either got his work in earlier today or just was in a little bit of an off day. We asked Shane Steichen after practice if uh the Colts head coach expected Pierce to be back on the field for the joint practices that they have with the Falcons on Wednesday and Thursday. Shane said that he did not um but seems like he's continuing to to progress well. We'll see if he gets on the field maybe for that final preseason game or if he works into things after the preseason is over with ahead of week one. Um as far as we know now he's still trending toward week one but no certainty on that um at the moment. So uh thanks for watching this Colts Insider video from Grand Park. Again, we'll be back uh here on Wednesday for a pair of joint practices with the Falcons before the teams face off in a preseason game on Saturday afternoon at Lucas Oil Stadium. Lot of stories going on at Indystar.com between now and Wednesday. Hope you guys check those out. Thanks for supporting and subscribing uh there and then of course continue to check out our YouTube channel um where we have all of our player interviews, some clips from practice as well as these Insider videos that we shoot every day. I'm Matthew Brown, he's Joel A. Erickson. Thanks for watching this recap from Colts training camp at Grand Park. >> Coach, how would you categorize the state of the defense? A lot of new guys, how is it all fitting into place so far? >> Yeah, it's coming together nicely. Um I like where our guys are at um Um, from a mental standpoint. I think they're taking heart to, you know, to lose playbook, um, making plays uh, day in and day out. Um, secondary's in a good spot. Um, the D-lines doing a hell of a job. Obviously having Buckner back and Grove and Lotulelei um, has been huge and Arden Key's coming on and Kevin Curry had a hell of a game in the preseason. So, I'm pleased with where those guys are right now. >> Is it easier to acclimate new guys on defense versus offense? They've heard certain language. It's really about the verbage and the technique that we're teaching. So, I think it goes both ways. >> What is the first thing that you would attribute to him so far? >> Toughness, a lot of physicality. You know, I'm young so they want me they want to see me play fast and aggressive. Just keep doing that. >> All right, thanks Jordan. >> Thanks, Jordan. >> Thank you. >> This uh linebacker room I think has a lot of competition going on guys too. Um kind of switching out for a lot of first team reps the last couple weeks of camp. What what uh is special about this group? >> Uh you know, I just think they did a great job up front of bringing in guys that are ready ready to compete. Um we've had competition throughout the years of me being here, but you know, this one is different because we got a lot of young guys that are hungry and who have uh the skill sets to to play right now. And so, you know, we push each other a lot in that linebacker room. It's great competition. Like we we're each other's biggest cheerleaders. Like we want to see each other do uh successful things. And you know, it's a great room and iron sharpens iron. That's our our mentality. And yeah, I mean, we come every day knowing that we got to compete cuz the next guy behind us is trying to take our job. >> What's going to surprise people about the Colts defense? >> Uh I think you know, it's not surprising to us, but it may be surprising to others it is the level of physicality that we that we're going to come and bring. And you know, for us that's a non-negotiable. That's one of the pillars of our defense is being uh physical and you know, we had it first last year of it. Uh that as as a whole as a whole defense that's our identity. You know, it starts with that and as linebackers that's what we hang our hats on is the ability to be physical and assert our dominance to the other team. >> You've seen a lot of new faces walk through the door and now it's all, you know, acclimating. How do you think it's all fitting together? >> I think it's fitting together well. I think, you know, we got a lot of, like I said earlier, a lot of people that are hungry for opportunity, a lot of good football players who know how to play the game, who are really coachable, um who want to compete and it makes it challenging because, like I said, you can't really have a bad day cuz everybody's hungry and everybody is looking for their chance to to move up on the depth chart. And that's how it's got to be. That's That's what's going to allow us to put the the best uh competitive advantage forward for our for the fans, the organization, and for the the team. >> Which of the two young guys in that linebacker room, um CJ, everyone knows he missed some some practices due to his injury, but back today, and then Bryce Specher, what particularly stands out about those two guys that has really impressed you so far today? >> I mean, they're they're both uh good in different ways. Bryce is just a He's a natural football player and he's super physical. He loves the game. He loves to run around. He brings juice and energy every day. I sit next to him in the meetings and, you know, he's over there just like I read his notes sometimes and it sometimes will make me laugh cuz he's just He's just young and hungry. And CJ, you know, he's great in his own in his own right. He has a little bit of an old soul. He's more uh you know, laid-back, but when it's time to go, like, he goes. And, you know, them two, they really feed off each other. And then on top of that, I mean, Wes Weeks and and Tosh, you know, those are guys that are are good too and and they they can play for us too. Devin as well. So, you know, it's a deep room and uh I like I love to see where where everybody stacks up. >> What what's it do for your confidence that, you know, a lot of defenses have two, three starters and it's kind of static, but with Lou and and Coach Specher, it's like you have four or five that you have played a ton of snaps. >> Yeah, I mean, confidence I think is the most important thing for any position. Um you got to have self-belief because if you don't, you know, the game is too hard to for you to be doubting yourself. If you don't believe in yourself, then, you know, you're you're not giving yourself the best advantage possible. So, for me that confidence is like I said not negotiable like it needs to be there no matter where where we are but at the same time when you getting first team reps and when you you know you're getting coached hard but you know there's high expectations and it's you know it makes you feel good and it does give me confidence. So, you know I love coach Lou and coach Bates have been doing a good job of instilling that in me and you know I got to keep taking steps forward and becoming the player that I know I can be. >> All right. Thanks Austin. >> How's the how's the competition on the back end is shaping up just generally right now? >> Um it's going great man. We got a lot of guys. A lot of guys can make plays. A lot of people can play. Um and honestly it brings out the best in you every day just because you really want to put your best foot forward every day. You know what I mean? Just everybody's pushing everyone you know but at the same time we hold everybody accountable. We we just kind of started something where it's just like I have our accountability board. If you you know you mess up with something in practice it's just something where you know nobody's sensitive. It's just you know it means more coming from the players you know what I mean than coaches all the time. So >> Do you guys point out these mistakes? >> Oh yeah. I mean the coaches obviously going to have their you know culture points but we see it on film. You know it's like jokingly but it's all love at the same time but you know just everybody wants everybody to play their best. >> So what happens on the accountability board? >> What happens board? What happens? >> Uh punishment you know you know it's this is like an internal thing you know what I'm saying? I can't give out give out a lot of juice but it's just like a little competition within all of us you know what I'm saying? But at the same time like it means more like I said coming from your peers than all the time you just hear from the coaches. So I just feel like it makes everybody better. >> Really broad question I mean what do you think your overall specifically is >> Um I feel like man I'm I'm I'm in bringing a different energy. Um just been I guess what they had last year, you know what I'm saying? I'm I'm a different person, you know, than whoever they had. Um and I just I have a lot of experience, you know, this my ninth year and I've been a bunch of different places, so I'm giving a different perspective to the coaches, uh players, like players that have only been here, you know what I mean? And um special teams as well. I'm I'm a dog on special teams, so um whatever the coaches ask me to do, man, more you can do that's pretty much been my career, so. >> I know Brian Mason mentioned that you might slide in with that pass personal protector role on special teams. Is that something you don't have a lot of experience with? >> Um I love it. Absolutely. Absolutely. Um I just feel like you're pretty much the captain of the special teams in a way and um I just like having that, you know, everybody uh listening to my calls and you're just pretty much running the show and that takes a lot of trust from the special team coach to have you there and um I just love that accountability. I love that pressure. And um I just consider myself a third gunner when I'm running down there especially. Um so I'm just trying to go in and do whatever I can make the team better. >> That perspective you just mentioned, you know, the more you can do and understanding your place and and staying power, is that something you share a lot with your younger teammates? >> Of course. Of course. And I mean they they see it from me every day. Like I said, um I pride on special teams. Like I don't like regardless who's going with the ones, twos, threes, like when we get to special teams, like it's that same energy, it's that same effort from me always, so um I just feel like that's that energy is contagious and anytime you step on that field, you're a starter in whatever role it is. Um and that's just uh the perspective I love, you know, and put especially with the younger guys, like AJ just him being able to see that and see that I'm year nine and I'm still doing all of this, you know what I mean? And I'm doing it at a high level, so um you know, I feel like it's good for everyone to see. >> What's the most impressive thing about AJ so far? >> Um ball skills, that's the biggest thing I I I noticed uh just cuz we're always doing work, you know, extra. Um ball skills are great, he's smart, you know, obviously there's like levels to the NFL and college, but I'm a lot carried over, but um that's the one thing I think he's going to just impress a lot of people with and his ball skills. He's real got hands. >> Looking ahead to joint practices this week, Sauce, what are some of the goals that you guys have or things you'd like to accomplish this >> Um just continue to build our culture and just keep building off the practices. Obviously, we're going to get some good players in here, you know what I mean? So, just be another good measuring stick for us, the secondary, up front, you know, they got running back, they got receivers. So, man, we excited. >> And that whole secondary and playing with Sauce Gardner, what what sticks out to you about him as a player, as a leader on and off the field? >> Um Sauce is very vocal even in the walk-throughs. He's always talking, always "I'll leverage, leverage," you And he's just sometimes younger guys seeing that and just seeing someone who has, you know, gotten to their second deal and just being so humble, talking to everybody just like he's just one of the guys, you know what I mean? And there's no Um because he made it so far in this aspect of his career is not, you know, no one acts like that. It's just That's the one thing I'll say, man, but his length, like press man, like his twitchiness, man, it's just be very exciting to play with Sauce. >> Can you talk to us about the journey you've kind of been on and taking pride doing all of the dirty work? Was there anybody in your career growing up that you looked at and was like, "Okay, this is where I can learn," but now you look up and you're that person? >> Um I mean, I've I've actually had a lot of vets that I played with, man. Mike Adams is one I played with him. He was I think Mike was year 16 my second year when I was in Houston. And I've had Mike Thomas, who's another guy that like a reserve safety. He actually played for Luke, Cincinnati, Miami, special teams. He'd come in dime packages and you know, I'm just young and like don't really know his story, but like the older I got and seeing, you know, he's in his 10th year whenever I was in Houston in my third year, you know, and I just never took those like conversations we had just learning from those guys and he was a PP as well. Uh Mike Thomas, so that's one thing I'll say, man. That was definitely a couple that stood out to me. >> Is this a kind of a unique situation at linebacker? Like there's been several of you guys cycling through with the ones. What what's that been like for you and what kind of opportunities is that have? >> Uh I think it just give everybody like a feel of like playing with different guys. I mean, yeah, it's the same for me, so I'm used to rotating throughout the camp cuz of injuries and stuff like that, uh but really get guys like we got a bunch of young guys, so when they need to catch catch up on things as the season is coming. So, just getting them up to speed, getting them playing with different guys. And really just make it making them communicate. I mean, if they usually if they ain't with me like it's a little bit easier just cuz I've been in the system for a long time, so just giving them a chance to like be out there beside each other, communicating, making all the calls, and just building up that that confidence, that leadership for the young guys. >> What's the competition like in that room as well? Those young guys that are fighting for time, some of them are >> I mean, they doing a good job. I mean, it's definitely a competitive group. You guys they I mean, they play hard, they play physical, and you just got to keep keep at it, keep learning. >> How does it feel like you're the old guy in the room? I mean, cuz you are. >> Yeah, I mean I mean, seeing that >> He's really old. YOU CAN'T SAY THAT. >> [laughter] >> HE'S THE experienced guy in the room. >> Yeah, I mean, seeing that I mean, he he he just now turned 21, so I'm like, damn. And some I mean, some of the guys coming in the league 24, I mean, so it made me kind of young, I mean, I'm I'm only 28, but like you said, experience while I've been in the league 7 years, so definitely guys coming in 1, 2, it's definitely a different feeling just being around a bunch of young guys. I mean, coming to me with advice and stuff like that, just make me feel old, you know? >> What did you gain from being a full-time starter last year in Arizona that maybe you can carry over to this year? >> Uh just experience. I mean, the more you more you out there, you just you know, honestly just keep learning and experience formations I mean a lot of times offenses kind of piggyback off each other. They might change up based off motions or just disguising it, but this uh this uh experience is being out there full time this you just seeing it things just come to you a little bit little bit better. >> How does playing with Blue now compare to when you were in Cincinnati? >> Uh, I think he's >> You're you're kind of a different player now than >> Yeah, yeah. I I I think Blue got a little soft since he came back. >> No, no, he's good dude. I mean I I love Blue. But I mean really I mean me and him kind of got like a a good relationship where like I can see the I see the my dad's a coach so I mean I I see the game through like a coach's lens a little bit so I mean me and him can like talk ball and I can give him like that on field feedback and he just we just piggyback off each other. >> How's your stuff been familiar with where does your dad coach and what did it ever get annoying that your dad >> Uh, yeah. I mean most definitely got annoying. >> I got and my phone got him saved as coach dad man it's it's ball dad it's dad second really. But uh I mean he's been all over. He he coached at Ball State back in when I was in middle school. Uh, he's at UVA right now. I mean so he's been coaching really all my life. >> All right. >> Thank you. Thank >> And you're still in the early stages of of camp and all that. Halfway through what what gives you optimism about this team? >> There's a lot of places I really like our depth. O-line, the way we're running the football right now. Uh I mean that that's fun to see. We went into New England and even the practices and games I mean we ran it really well. Now we didn't hold onto it like we should have, but it's just you look around there's a number of places. I mean uh you know, the young safety he's exciting. Halsey and then McGallon those two guys right now are really sticking out big time. >> What's C.J. Allen missing right now? Like do Do anticipate he'll still be able to kind of hit the ground running when he does return? >> I think so. I mean, he's a smart guy. He played in a in a complicated defense in college. So, I mean, he's still in all the meetings. Now, yeah, it kind of hurts missing some of that live Everybody likes to do it real speed, you know, but I mean, as soon as he gets back, he's just going to have to take the or really rely on all those mental reps he's been getting and get it running, but he I know he's he's busted his butt trying to get back and he's going to >> You mentioned offseason and young. What stands out to you about those two guys? >> I mean, the same things we saw in the draft, really. I mean, they're both even though it's totally different positions, right? They're both really tough, they're really physical, and they can both run fast. >> What have you made of what's been your perspective of Keenan Allen just recovering, how he's looked early on in camp, where he's moving around? >> He did an incredible job rehabbing, the same with our medical staff, cuz it doesn't I mean, there's him and then Wally, like it You like, "What happened?" It didn't even happen to him. Right. So, they both look like they did previously. >> When you look at wide receivers, how do you prioritize traits? >> Uh I think it's like, you know, I've always looked at it like putting together a basketball team, right? You have those different body types and sizes, like you got a point guard, which, you know, you got Josh Downs, you know, and then you got small forward, a power forward. I mean, that's what you're trying to do cuz there's just there's different plays for every guy, there's there's scheming it up for different people in different situations, and you want to have those different body types and not just all the same guy. >> Does it Does a proven depth at that position bother you? >> Uh I mean, we're going to keep looking, but the guys, you know, like Nick's played a lot of football, as well as Quentin Johnston. And then Tread has been around a long time, and I know, you know, first-round pick, he probably hasn't had the career he's hoped, but we're counting on those two guys to come in and contribute. And then, I mean, we're going to keep looking, too, just like we always do. >> So, for you, it's still pass for me. Obviously, Keenan Allen is still out there. >> Yeah, it always is. >> How do you feel about linebacker just kind of evolving right now, that position generally? >> Well, going back to CJ when he gets back, that'll make it a little more clearer, but there's guys like um you know, Austin you know, he's always had the athleticism but but like the game just seemed fast forward for a while, now it's looks like it's really slowed down. Um you know, we we talked about Chambers back in May. Uh last, I mean, some of those young guys have traits that and they're not household names, but you're just hoping they can come in and ascend and then Keem Davis Gabe who's played a lot of ball. and then uh you know, Feuchters coming on and you see his physicality. So, yeah, it's not the household names, but they make some nervous, but you know, you got to roll dice sometimes. >> And how do you weigh the potential for an Anthony trade versus quarterback depth which is pretty precious? >> Well, I think you take care of your own team first. >> And that's uh >> Does that answer? >> Depth chart matters? I mean, we we would have three that could play. he's one of them, he's going to be here. >> What are what are the pros and cons of of having three? Just Chris has expressed that that was his ultimate desire to keep all three. >> Look at last year. yeah, I mean, you never know. >> And if somebody says after 3 years Anthony is here where is he after 3 years and why isn't he further or or whatever. >> Uh it's a number of factors. I mean, a lot of it's probably been injuries. Uh you know, he was really raw coming in and you know, that stunted it. Every time he kind of got going, he got hurt. Uh but he's working hard out here and we're just going to keep evaluating it. He's going to keep getting better. >> Is there any last question? >> Any update on Alex Erickson? We have seen him a little bit more out here individually, but do you have any update on Alex? >> He's doing good. He's working hard. I'm not concerned about Allen. >> I appreciate it.

title: Houston Texans' Sunday practice insights, assistant coach intel
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. Texans Sunday training camp practice as they get ready for the Las Vegas Raiders preseason game this week preceded by a joint practice and this was a big-time workout especially for Pro Bowl corner Kamari Lacader just absolutely textbook fundamental techniques put on a show in the one-on- ons that the way he punches the football out the way that he shadows receivers just an outstanding day for him and good news in the secondary. Jaylen Petri back to practice after missing most of last week with a minor injury was undisclosed. So they get back, you know, Jaylen Petri is the hammer, the hard-hitting nickel that you want to have there. And obviously, uh, training camp is training camp. You want him when the games count, but he is back and they eased him in a day away from team drills. uh you did not have Tank Dell out there. I think it was a rest day. Seems like there's been no setback or anything alarming. And then when you think about, you know, Jaylen Null, the receiver, it's not just his right pinky. Talked to Ben McDaniels about this. It's also his hamstring and says he's doing a good job of working his way back. Uh the timetable is a couple of weeks. So it's a setback for Jaylen Null, the projected starting slot receiver. If he's not ready for the first game, and I think he still will be under this timetable, but if he wasn't, Xavier Hutchinson would step into that slot role. They feel very good about his ability to line up at so many different positions. So that is something to keep an eye on, obviously. And then uh since we're talking about injuries, others, I said, Tank Dell, no practice. Jaylen Null, no practice. Jammarcus Ingram can't practice with uh dislocated shoulder that he sustained against the in the preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers. So Colin Wright uh they like what they were seeing from him. Talked to Dino Alvaso. You'll hear from several assistant coaches interviews. I'm going to bring those to you. Uh but you know he has got a soft tissue injury. He is dayto-day. And then Jake Hansen ran on a side field. Progress from him from his ankle as we've been talking about. He's making progress. So, he's in the mix still for third linebacker when he gets back out there. Reverend Jordan is still not practicing due to a knee injury and they had hoped to get him back as soon as this week and he's still not back out there and obviously not a good sign that they signed former University of Connecticut tight end. Lewis Hansen also played at Michigan. Hansen, a big tight end, rookie, undrafted guy, sort of a practice squad candidate, and uh reported that story this morning that Hansen had rejoined the team. He was with them previously. Still no Jir Jordan strained hip flexor and British Brooks, a broken hand. British is in a cast. Have not seen Jaw since the injury. Noah Winnington continues to be the third back in drills. So, we'll go through some of the things that happened and then we'll segue to have you guys hear from these, you know, assistant coaches. Cole Papovich, the Texans offensive line coach run game coordinator, tells me that he hasn't picked his starting five yet. He says the starting five we saw against the Panthers might not be the starting five. So there's still some chance obviously I think for Trent Brown who they are very comfortable with as he competes with Braden Smith for the right tackle job. But yeah I mean interesting the left tackle. We know about Wyatt Teller of course left guard. Lots of praise for Keelin Rutled their prize rookie first round draft pick. He's very happy with the aggressiveness and conscientiousness attention to detail that he's seen from him throughout camp and also just that carrying out in that preseason game. And besides Rutled know he's pleased with Urser's improvement where he's come from a year from now. Although Ed Ingram has been beaten for some plays including Shel Rankings being for sack the other day. He says Ingram he tells him hey you were third team at this time last year. Look at you now. So I think they're trying to do everything possible to bring him along and I think some of it's just still a byproduct for a lot of these offensive linemen. It's not easy for them. They're playing against the absolute best defense and then uh yeah, let's go through some of more of the the drills things we saw. So, you know, looking at, you know, what happened as I said, Kamar Lassner, outstanding practice. I thought that Jared Wayne, who's had the touchdown, of course, against the Chargers stacked another good practice. Davis Mills hits him with excellent timing and he goes up and gets it over Jaylen Smith. And then Lewis Bond a touchdown about half the football field he traveled going over the middle splitting Kamari Lassner and Caleb Bulock. CJ Stra delivered that throw. So that was good. And then you know I feel like Jaden Higgins against Jaylen Smith very competitive situations but Higgins won that with Stingley and Nico Collins. We're watching one-on- ones in the red zone and the first play Derek Stingley Jr. got a punch out knocking the football away from Nico Collins, but Nico won the second one. So, we were watching that and I think it was just interesting to watch how that goes. Um, it was a Foster Maro touchdown and u can't really describe the play uh for competitive reasons, but he did well and we still see CJ Strad throwing to Jaden Higgins. Not a lot of big runs. It's tough. The screen plays aren't going very well. Um, we're seeing the defense still have tackles for losses on David McGomery. We saw a decent scramble by CJ Strad. So, that was something to note. And yeah, just in watching the guys and seeing how they're doing, um, I thought it was kind of a good back and forth, a competitive day. It wasn't like the defense dominated, but there was still some moments there for the defense where it was very tough. But yeah, I mean there was one Woody Marks 4-yard run. There was a David Montgomery 11 yard run mixed in. So, uh, they had some progress, especially early and then it kind of caught up to them a bit. The, you know, defense having a good day overall. But, yeah, I think you look at this and kind of where things are as a team. It, it's an interesting situation. And we'll go through It is hot out here still. They cut the air conditioner off. Uh, I'm here uh last man standing here of the press corps of the beat. Uh, but I'm here and I'm here for you guys to talk some football. So, it's not like I had to play football in this. I'm just watching and yeah, so I'll go through some things that I'm seeing. So, Ben McDaniels, we're bringing the conversation with Ben and we'll kind of go back and forth a little bit about some of these convos that we had as we go through some of these situations. obviously still competitive for a lot of spots, but yeah, you'll hear from Ben McDaniels about Tank Dell and about the ascension of Jaden Higgins. And we saw that again today, the arrow being up and they expect a lot from him. So, they're seeing good things from him, of course, uh happy with Lewis Bond and everything with Xavier Hutchinson, Jared Wayne. So, it's been a good camp for the receivers and there were other years where it wasn't so good. So, I think there's progress there. So, we will bring you that conversation now. Kind of I think that's a good way. We'll go back and forth as I set the stage for some of these interviews. Of course, this is brought to you by my friends at Fencegeeks at fence geeks.com. Call a lawyer if you've been in an accident. And remember guys, they work in contingency. They don't get paid until you get paid. And they fight and they win for you. And they are, of course, great members of the community here in Houston, Texas. All right, guys. Without any further ado, there will be practice videos. I'll show you some of these one-on- ones I've been describing. And also, you're going to hear right now from Texans receivers coach and pass game coordinator Ben McDaniels. And then we're going to pivot to the offensive line. >> In the spring, you were talking about Tank and your encouragement. What have you seen from Tank since camp started? Kind of just excited for his process to keep going. You know, his uh his attitude's been great and how he comes into the building uh every day. You know, ready to uh progress and and keep working along his process. >> You seeing that arrow up for Higgins year two? >> Uh yes and yes. And another yes. And uh null um was saying that hamstring uh had a little bit set back with that on top of the pinky. What's the kind of big picture for him? What do you think it'll take? >> Um I expect him when he hits the grass to be ready to roll. He's extremely uh diligent with his preparation and and uh being ready to go when he's going to be healthy. Coach, >> can you talk about the consistency and improvement of Jerry Wayne? >> Um quite quite honestly, he has a lot of consistency since he's been in our building. Um and uh he's fighting for for every opportunity he gets and uh trying to make the most of him. Um you know he's he's uh his preparation is terrific. He comes out here and competes and uh some of the fruits of that are showing up in particular about Higgins has caught your eye. Everybody's talking about this this big leap that he's taken. His body was a little bit different as well. I think I think in I think in year two like there's a confidence that you should probably have developed through the first year that shows itself in year two that like nothing's really new anymore. And like you can see that from him, you can feel that from him. And um I mean he's he's extremely intelligent as it is. And so for him to stack, you know, a whole bunch of confidence and experience and build on that, it's kind of showing itself >> with that confidence. And how much more confident has he allowed you to be in moving him around a little bit inside, outside? >> Uh Come on, baby. All right, guys. There is receivers coach Ben McDaniels, the passing game coordinator for the Texans. But let's hear from Cole Papovic now. And everybody wants to know about the offensive line and his thoughts. Cole is the offensive line coach and the run game coordinator and what he thinks about Ariata Ursery and that starting unit that they had out there against the Los Angeles Chargers in particular comments about their first round draft pickage and he was talking about Ed Ingram and it was interesting to hear his thoughts on Trent Brown who has also played some left tackle and his thoughts on his ability to play left tackle in a pinch. He is their swing tackle and yes, they have Blake Fischer, but you know, Trent in 2018 when he was with the Patriots and Cole was up there, they won it all with him as their left tackle blocking for the great Tom Brady. So, that's interesting to watch, you know, his ability to play on both sides. And of course, no one's bigger. He said it, we've said it, he is lighter and leaner. So Trent Brown has worked very hard to get in good shape and do everything that he needs to do to prepare himself for the season. The big thing with Trent, the big man, biggest offensive lineman, massive in the NFL, is that he's healthier right now. And that does help a lot to have a healthy Trent Brown. So you need that. You want to see Trent at his best. And right now, that's what they're seeing from Trent. They're having a healthier Trimp Brown. All right. And uh right after Cole, we'll of course have, you know, other coaches that I spoke with, including defensive line coach Rod Wright. So, I'll set the stage for that as well. Having Janavian Clowney is obviously an impact signing, three-time Pro Bowl pass rusher, former top overall draft pick, someone that has done it in the NFL, is an accomplished pass rusher and runs stopper, makes third downs very challenging for the defense. We've already seen a lot of success for JD Clowney, number 90 out here on the field. I had a good conversation with him about Ken McDonald. A couple false steps, only a couple tackles, but he sees pretty good twitchiness. This is from Rod Wright, the defensive line coach, run game coordinator, coaches, the big rookie from Ohio State, their second round draft pick, a former Big 10 Conference defensive line of the year. So, we'll hear from him about Katie McDonald and also about Solomon Bird making some noise, has had a good camp, and these guys, you know, he says it's an honor and a privilege for them that they're counted on to have no drop off whenever they sub out the Will Anderson Juniors, the Denil Hunters, and the Damian Klein.
