Uh, he's kind of set the led the way and set the tone for us. um the all the goals that we had from the spring I feel like accomplishing a pre- snap standpoint um and now it's just going and executing postnap wise and um he's done a great job of that. He's in good shape. Uh he looks good physically. Uh he's kind of uh just kind of leading the charge in there in the huddle at the line of scrimmage mixing up cadences and executing. Proud of him the way Trent Trent mentioned that felt like last year stuff wasn't getting out of the huddle in a timely manner. like this year they're breaking the huddle in a good amount of time. What kind of has CJ done to make sure that's been they they have more time to line scrimmage. >> Um I don't know that I I wouldn't say it's probably like oh he's put in more time. It's just probably I would say year two and everything sounds a lot more familiar. Uh he probably took it upon himself this year in the offseason to make sure he's good on all the verbiage, all the calls and you can kind of anticipate the calls as they're coming in. We trust with all those guys to just, you know, read the call sheet, keep reading the call sheet, understand being able to finish the play as it's coming in. And, uh, I would say that's probably the biggest thing is, uh, we're getting it in quicker, we're getting it called quicker, and we're up to the line with a lot of time to do. >> Feels like he's executing really well when you guys face a tough defense every day, but when there's pressure, messy pockets, have you kind of seen that growth and improvement there? Uh, I don't know that I would say in uh growth cuz I think he's always done well, but he has done continued to do an excellent job moving in the pocket. Uh, Justin around stepping up in the pocket, but also keeping his eyes downfield and making the throws as opposed to just always scrambling. You always tell them, "Hey, if you can step up, keep your eyes downfield cuz you got a shot to make the right one." The younger quarterback learning this system, is there is there a lot more to the pass protection than you guys have handled playoffs on a lot of systems? Um the quarterback. >> Yeah. Yeah. I don't know that there's a lot more per se. There might just be something that's a little bit different that they've done. So if you want to say that it's a little bit of a new learning, uh maybe that's part of it. But I do feel like once once you kind of go and get the hang of it, then it's been old hat a little bit. Now we've got a new quarterback that just came in, so kind of going through that process of him. I feel like CJ and Davis are really comfortable in right now. To me, it's the only way I can build the bottom half of my roster in the linebacker room is my world. So, I know Aziz and Henry. I know where they are, and I have to have them ready for the season. But, I've got to find out which one of these eight other guys can make our team and can play defense the way we want them to play defense. Well, this is invaluable. Like, I need them to get all the reps they can in the games. I don't care if the starters play at all. They've got 17 games that they've got to go ahead and put on the line. It is hard to make it 17 games playing linebacker the right way. You don't need the preseason to really bang your body up too much, right? We have to get ready for game one in the season. The rest of the guys I need every preseason. I wish we had four again because that's once the season starts those those backups, they don't get any reps. They barely get practice reps. So, you really develop the depth of your whole team in training camp and in preeason. So, those young guys have to play. They have to be our guys. >> What have you seen from Wade? What has this this training camp been standing out physically? >> Yeah, Wade's a great example of he needs to play a lot more NFL ball to to get him to calm his mind down. You know, it's not much different than college other than the talent takes a big step up, which means the speed takes a big step up, which means you have to play with a clear mind. But we're in the NFL now and we have more because that's our profession all day. That's all we have is football, not school and football. So that's why we Wade's done a nice job, but he just needs to play more. >> Humble's one of the new faces that you guys have. He's got a lot of special teams experience, but getting him caught up on the defense. How's that going? >> It's going well. Again, he needs more reps. More rep and the preseason reps and we can give them uh the team practice reps. That's that's how you get better playing football by playing football and playing at the fastest speed you can play and tackling to the ground because number one job we have is tackle the guy with the ball to the ground. So in order to do that and get good at it, you have to play in the preseason games. >> Those preseason games kind of like a buffet for linebackers. It feels like they get a lot of opportunities, kind of more simple runs. Guys aren't deep in the offense and opportunities to cover as well. >> Yeah, it it is simpler in the preseason because the offense is evaluating their guys like we are. Let's keep it simple. Let's see how good they are. Techniques and size, speed, do they play the game of football well? uh or they just highweight speed guys. So, we have to kind of evaluate all those things. So, it helps when the offense stays simple and we stay simple. So, both of us can evaluate and pick our teams, right? >> How great is it to know Henry sticking around the contest? >> Oh, I was so happy. I was I was happy when Z signed and I I mean, they're great guys. They they earned everything they put the work in. And there's nothing more rewarding than a coach is when guys are putting the work in and they get rewarded because a lot of times some talented guys that don't work real hard get rewarded. And it's awesome when guys like Henry Aiz get rewarded because they put the work in. You get what you earn and they've earned it. >> Talking to Wade the other day, he said sometimes the other defenders give the linebackers a little bit of a hard time because they're coach Ryan's favorites. You got to kind of be a buffer with those other defenders. Hey, get off my >> I don't know. I don't have favorites. A lot of goes with that favorite. Now you got the eyes on you the most too now. Maybe our favorite, but he's he's in and he's coaching. Demo couldn't have been a better. He's so it's so great when he comes in the room and shares with the guys 10 years of experience of hands-on playing and it's his scheme. So now we've got his scheme. So it and he's he's always been fun around. Domo is one of the best guys I've ever coached and now that I'm coaching with him, it's an honor and and it's a it's a blessing. We have a lot of good linebacker knowledge to help these linebackers grow >> to step in and try and absorb all that right away. It's really difficult like you're still drinking from the uh you know fire hose however many months it is. So for a young guy like Marlin to be able to just say hey there's a lot of stuff out there honing in on maybe one particular thing each day. It's really easy to say to do that. It's really difficult for a young guy who wants to help the team do the right things. Um so again like speaks of his character. That's what draws you to guys like Marlin, like Kane. And then you even look even further like I could put Brev in that like Brev had a hard road here where like injuries then he had a little hiccup here the other week where he's working through something but he's still in the means. He's still taking the coaching. It's a really good room where it's just high character guys. It makes my job really easy. >> With Marlin in particular, where is he stronger at it picking some of those things up on the NFL level and where's he still maybe have a little room to grow? >> Yeah, I think that for him in the route running like he's trying to figure out, okay, where do I fit in? He's not like G. He's not like Foster. He's not like Bre. Like they're all different. So it's hard for those guys to say, "Okay, hey, just run the route like him." Like that's not necessarily always the case. And he's got to go out there. He's got to rep it. He's got to be in making a mistake and then be willing to come back and try something new, which is difficult, especially on a big stage like an NFL training team. Man, the run game, it's all for him, man. It's been very new. He's never played in a mic point driven system like this before. So every day is a learning experience for him. And again, he does a really good job of taking the coaching, um, watching veterans, taking input from veterans, and then again, most importantly, he listens to the coaches. >> As far as routes, how do you how do you get them to work on that? Is it just like reps or is it can you have any particular like I don't know other players that have played in the league that you give him film to kind of emulate? >> And that's the thing, you try and show them like, okay, hey, maybe a bigger guy, you know, uses his body to create a little bit more separation some of these routes. Okay. Now, look at these guys who use their savviness to get open, right? like you don't always see the fastest guys, you know, getting open with speed. But Marvin has this and interesting ability where he can use speed, but also he has size where he can body someone up and create a little separation. So, he's got a unique skill set. He's got to watch other guys games, take what from them what might work for him, and then at the same time, like if it doesn't work for him, he's got to go ahead and throw it out and try the next tool. >> Are there any ones in particular that you put pointed off for >> Marlin? Yeah, it's been a gamut of guys. Like I like him watching Dole, but then you put on old Jason Whitten film. There's some savviness in the way Jason Whitten set up leverage on defenders. Then you look at Rob like Donowski, right? Using his size on guys, right? And then you look at someone maybe like George KD who's not exactly like a blazer, but he's kind of like a bully in his routes. So it's like, okay, Marlin, this works for them. I'm not saying it's necessarily going to work for you, but just how everyone adapts the game to their styles. Speaking of adapting, uh, when you look at him and as far as his athleticism and his mindset and him wanting to be, uh, you know, more of a physical force out there, because last week Keen Rage called him a dog. He said, "When I look at him, he, you know, he has all those intangibles. How are you able to hone that type of stuff in and help him, you know, um, excel on the next level?" >> Yeah. So, like, you know, when we look for guys in our room, like there's non-negotiables. They got to be tough. They got to be team first. And then at the end of the day, they got to have finish. And so like if you don't have those three things, you're probably not going to be on the Houston Texans. So like those guys check those boxes right away. Now once you get to the field, okay, can I understand what my assignment is, how to execute it, and then play the way we expect them to play. Um it's a process, but yeah, th those are intangibles that all those guys have. Um we preach it, but again, like if it's not in their blood, they wouldn't be in those seats to begin with. >> What is it like having a offensive coordinator who's a former tight end's coach? >> It's great. Um, for me selfishly, I've never coached a position, so I have an incredible resource 30 ft away. Hey, Nick, like, how are we seeing this? How do you want this to look? You've done this before. Hey, we're going down to one-on- ones in the red area. I kind of want to see Marlin work this. What do you think? Like, you're talking about an incredible resource that I have 30 ft away. Um, for me, I I've really enjoyed it. I've I really enjoyed Nick. Um, he's been incredibly helpful. I can't be more thankful. Anything else? Tay, it's been a productive training camp for you so far. You rush every block every day against Will Anderson Jr., Denil Hunter, and all those guys. What's that like for you? How does that help you improve? Uh, I think it helps me improve a lot, you know, just going out there being coachable. Um, whatever coach presents to me, just going out there being able to attack it against some good guys, you know, every day. So, um, so far the training camp, I feel like I'm, you know, I'm getting better and more confident at my ability and what I'm capable of doing. >> What's the move that you're getting better at really counteracting when they try that move, whether it might be a long arm or speed rush? What do you feel like you're getting better at? Which which punches >> win or lose? I'm I'm really trying to work on my punch. >> Yeah, >> that's like the biggest thing. uh not successfully last year. So, I feel like if I'm coming out here and trying to consistently punch against these two guys, you know, I feel like I'm I'm I'm going to be in a good a good direction, but you know, I'm not it's not going to always be pretty, you know, a ugly win, still a win, you know. So, um just trying to go out here and be productive and be, you know, accountable and have consistency. >> How do you define success for yourself individually? >> Um really just being consistent, bro. you know, playing at a high level. Um, like I said, have getting training against some of the best guys against the league, you know, you get out there, it's like, you know, Denil, he mentioned, we always always have conversations, you know, he like, man, when you get out there, it's going to be a breeze, you know. So, you know, knowing that, putting that in the back of my mind makes me, you know, feel more comfortable. >> The first game under your belt, you guys got out there together as a unit. How much was that kind of uh reassuring just to see, hey, what we were doing in practice as an offensive line that carried over? >> I think it was definitely good for us to go out there in a live setting against another team that we've been going against each other all camp. So, it was kind of refreshing to uh go out there and punch another team in the face >> with uh Kevlage, you were in his shoes last year. Do you impart any advice? Doesn't look like he maybe needs as much advice. Seems like a a ready kind of rookie and uh ready to go. Yeah, I guess if it calls for that, >> what do you see? >> What was the question? >> What do you see from Rage? He you were in his shoes a year ago as the rookie starter. Now he's with the ones as a rookie. What do you see from him? Just kind of mentality and how he's doing. >> You know, I see a guy that uh definitely fits the culture, you know, a swarm mentality. Um that's going to come out there and give it his all. Um is very intentional with the details and as a young player, like it's good to see that. Um, and I I don't see nothing but how successful >> the season. You guys have high expectations. You've never shied away from that. What do you sort of look at the season kind of the approach of what it will take to do the what you want the big deep playoff run, Super Bowl, all those things? Yeah, that's that's later down the line. But each week, you know, we just want to go one and0. >> Um, every week, whatever, however that looks like, how muchever work we got to put in, we all know the the importance of it, and it starts right here in training camp. So, you know, every day we just out there trying to attack that goal. >> Are you bigger, stronger, leaner? What are some things that you feel like you're better at? >> Definitely feel like I'm a little bit stronger um in all areas really. I've been working out since the end of February. Uh really just like I said, trying to get my body stronger, get the mental uh stronger, you know, having balance too, taking a break. Um hanging out with the fam. Uh it's, you know, slowly getting back into it. >> Some kind of responsibility goes with being the left tackle, protecting the quarterback's blind side. How much is that something feels like kind of a privilege and a challenge because that's uh where they put up a lot of the best rushers? >> I did a lot of a lot in college, you know, in the pros. cuz I'm just trying I'm trying to have a lot of success. So, I know the importance of that every day just, you know, what type of mental you got to have uh to go out here and play at a high level. You know, it takes a certain type of cat, a certain type of guys to come out here to protect CJ um and give him time, you know, so he can be successful as well. So, um, you know, so far as a unit, I feel like, you know, we out here attacking everything, you know, the details of Coach Pop, um, the meeting rooms, you know, and, um, like I said, man, I I couldn't ask for a better group of guys. >> It's like the movie The Bodyguard. That's you. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> Um, playing for Coach Pop, the intensity. We can hear him and, you know, we've gotten to know him some now after a few years. What's it like playing for him? Is it Is it fun? Is it also like, hey, we don't want to let coach down. What's it like playing football? >> Yeah, I feel like every coach got pride, you know, every coach got pride over their players. You know, Coach Pav is definitely one of those guys. And uh, you know, we just don't want to go out there and, you know, uh, let each other down, not let anybody let nobody on the offense down, you know, and then everything starts with the whole line. >> So, um, just going out there, holding each other accountable, man, playing at a high level, and really being transparent with ourselves. you and Wyatt now that you're teaming up there. What do you learn from him? Because he's played a lot of football. He's been in the Pro Bowl. He's done all that. >> Uh what I really learned from Wyatt, man, is you know, have fun, take care of your body. Um you know, try to have like find some fun in this. You know, campus are already hard enough, you know. Uh he's definitely been a guy enjoy, you know, to be around and the guys here love them. And I saw your I don't know if you call it a cheap meal or just a regular meal, but you guys I saw Pitt Room. It was a what? Brisket, sausage. What did you get? >> Yeah, we went to uh Pit Room >> and uh Pinkerton. >> Pinkerton. Two barbecues. Wow. >> Two barbecue spots. It's a uh my first time. >> Okay. >> Clear the area. My first time trying it. >> Uh I'm really a loyal fan of KC Barbecue. >> Yeah. So I try to shy away from you know Houston Texas barbecue >> like Jack Stack those those places like that Sunny's good ones. >> Exactly. So no but it was actually pretty good though you know and spend some time with Wyatt you know and uh really get to hang around him and you know see his personality. >> Yeah. You meet him, meet his family. Yeah. You can bond over a group like that. Last one for you. When we talked last year when you got here you had that perspective. It wasn't easy for you coming up. your mom and you guys sacrificed a lot. You mean your all your siblings. Do you kind of hit yourself every now and then and say, "Hey, man, I've come a long way, not just on the field, but what that's done for you off the field and for your family." >> Yeah, man. I feel like that'll never go nowhere. You know, I try to show that, embody that every day, you know, have my chip on my shoulder. Um, and like I said, I've been carrying that with me since I started sports, period. You know, basketball, track, wrestling, whatever it was, you know, I just try to go out there and be the best and really, you know, have something my family could look forward to, you know, uh, you know, being an athlete or whatever the case may be, you know, just trying to make them proud and, uh, continue to try to be the best brother, the best son, the best uncle, you know, that my family could ask for, you know. So I got, you know, my family I hold dear to my heart, you know, and also my faith too, you know, really close with God, praying and uh really believing, having, you know, a strong faith. >> Absolutely. Say, thanks for your time and good luck this season.

title: Detroit Lions players meet with the media | 2026 Training Camp Day 13
text: How do you how do you stack up against the rest of the league in your mind? >> Us as a core? >> Yeah. >> I think we're the best in the league. I mean, obviously Jamo and Saint are the proven veteran guys who have gone out there every single Sunday and made plays and you know, I've been trying to make my name and I think the three of us together, you know, it's going to be hard to stop all of us. >> How will your role kind of differ in terms of where you're going to be positioned at >> Yeah, I mean, it kind of just depends on scheme, game plan. Obviously, you know, in the base stuff out here for training camp, you know, we're trying to spread the ball around a little bit. You know, in 11 personnel, 13, you know, just trying to spread the ball around, get get the ball in guys' hands. >> You made a catch in double coverage and that little spike there. Was that a like a Were you looking for a for a play like that all all preseason or what? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, there's definitely been opportunities for me to make plays like that. So, the fact that JG put the trust in me on fourth down like that, put the ball up in the air, you know, he's been waiting for me to win on the release like that. So, just the fact that I was able to do that, stack the guy and he threw a perfect ball where I can go up and get it. So, things just shook out greatly and you know, it was nice to score on fourth down like that. >> Do you marvel sometimes at how often Alshon Jeffery can just make make any catch any position and wherever his body is, no matter who's covering him. Does he just marvel >> It is it is [laughter] it is mind-blowing. Like I'll be behind him in one-on-ones. And like it looks like he got beat or he's getting pushed to the sideline and he'll just be running like this and next thing you know, just late hands and he catches it. Like sometimes I'm just like that's stupid. Like you should not be able to do that. He's just incredibly talented and catches everything. >> When you're looking at the mention making a name for yourself to be able to pull in a pass like that for a touchdown, just how good does it feel coming off the preseason game? >> Yeah, it feels great. Um, you know, I want to continue to build confidence in myself, in JG and this offense, the coaching staff. I just like want to continue putting stuff on film even if it's not catching, whether it's you know, blocking or even if I'm not even getting the rock running the running the route, winning, blocking, turning up field, just doing everything I can, uh, you know, to build confidence in this offense. >> Any conversations with Scotty after that play off to the side? >> This one over here? No, he's he you know, he just likes to hype me up. He just gave me a big old high five and I'm sure he'll say something about it in meetings. That's when I'll talk to him. >> What have those conversations been like maybe a little bit different this off season for you? >> Yeah, I think just the expectations for me are heightened that much where I need to be on my game every single day, you know. Last year I could have maybe an excuse, you know, I'm a rookie, I'm new to this offense, but this year, you know, it's time for me to step up, um, and make plays just like that, uh, every single day. >> Hey Isaac, how how much did Thursday kind of stick in your craw and then how quickly do you just flush it and move on to the next practice? Like what's that balance like for you? >> Yeah, I mean you got to flush it right away. Obviously, you know, the big thing for me is I can catch the football, there's no doubt about that. So, I'm not worried about that. I think, you know, the biggest thing for me is winning on the releases and running good routes and, you know, making sure I'm open. I feel like I did that well, so it's just a matter of finishing the play, which has never been a problem for me in my football career. >> You spiked that one in the end zone. Touchdown at the end of the spike. Was that what some frustration out of >> No, that's just kind of tradition. If we score, we spike it. So, yeah. >> On that that route, did you feel like you won on the release? Obviously, you weren't going up to get it, but was that just kind of a a snapshot of how you wanted it to look this season from start to finish? >> Yeah, for sure. Like I've been trying to be a little bit quicker with my releases, uh, cuz you know, they expect me to be a bigger guy and get into them. So, if I'm able to shed them at the line and just get vertical, JJ can really put the ball anywhere and that's been my goal and obviously JJ threw a great ball. >> You okay to get banged up a little >> Yeah, yeah. Nothing serious. I'm all good. >> What was it like first day back in pads, the first time in a while? >> Uh, it felt good. Uh, just getting the rust off a little bit. Uh, was out for a week, but it felt a lot longer, so felt good to be back out there. >> What kind of benchmarks do you want to see yourself hit before the second preseason game? >> Uh, just getting better, uh, with the with the rhythm of the offense, uh, being at center now and just getting the chemistry down with JJ and just continuing to get reps and hopefully we get the chemistry down by the end of the preseason cuz I know it's uh it takes time. So, just getting the reps together with him. And yeah, that's my goal. >> That rain, the wet ball, did that play with the snaps at all for you guys today? >> Uh a little bit, but that's no excuse, you know, that's good work for us, wet ball, cuz it's going to happen in the season. So, it's always good work. The first wet ball practice is, you know, it's going to be some balls on the ground for sure. >> JC, you played a lot of last season, but you also played some some pretty good center in the NFL and in college. Can you explain just maybe your comfort there and how much you're looking forward to maybe getting a chance to play center again? >> Yeah, definitely comfortable uh for sure. Um like you said, played in college, played a little bit in the league. Definitely comfortable uh new offense, you know, it's a little different, but getting used to it. Just like I said, I need reps and I'm getting those now, so we'll be ready to go for sure. >> What do you think your strengths are at the center position? >> Uh just my quickness, uh quickness, my get-off. And uh just being having everybody on the same page. I feel like I do a good job of that, but it's always room for improvement. >> What were you dealing with that kept you out? >> Uh I don't want to disclose that, but nothing serious, minor injury. >> Would you call center your natural position? >> I guess you could say that, yeah. Uh I wouldn't say natural because I didn't play it till I got to college, so I mean, wherever you need me, I'mma play, but definitely more comfortable at center. >> JC, what was your reaction to the trade when it went down this offseason and what kind of opportunity did you see for yourself here? >> Yeah, I was shocked for sure. Uh you know, you never you never know when it's going to happen, but uh definitely excited when I heard it was Detroit cuz I remember we came here for a joint practice last year and I remember the environment and it was it was really cool. So, I was definitely excited once I learned it was Detroit and I'm just happy to be back in the Midwest. >> You played a little more center than Tate, you know, he's newer to the position, I guess. Is there any What sort of talk goes on on the sideline in terms of >> Man, man, yeah, just tell him to to not get down on himself, you know, cuz it's going to be bad plays like I said wet ball. So, it's going to be some bad snaps, but just move on to the next play and I told him like just have the guys on the same page. If you're all If you're all wrong, we're all right. So, just just trying to encourage him cuz I know how it is being a young guy at >> You've been around this team and in this group of offensive lineman just for a little bit now, but what have you seen from the depth, the talent, just the youth and what this position group really could offer? >> Uh I'm excited. Uh like you said, we got a lot of youth. Uh a lot of guys growing, getting better each day and I'm just excited to be around guys like like Tate, Christian, uh Penei, of course. Uh just excited to play with these guys and you can just feel the energy with them. Uh they It's a youthful energy. So, it's definitely cool uh being around guys my age. So, uh yeah, I'm excited. >> What about the opportunities that today presents, you know, no Jay Moore today. So, you get to run with some first team reps. Just how important are those? How much do you value that those opportunities? >> Uh it's great, honestly. Get out there on with the ones and just um you know what I mean, get a chance to go against the one defense and um get some reps with Jared and all those other guys. It's just great opportunity for me and to get my feet wet and um play some ball, move fast with those guys, you know. >> Have you heard the comments Dennis made about you the last couple days? >> No, not I've been I've been trying to like stay laser focused, kind of like them um horses, trying to keep them blinders on, just stay stay accorded. Um just keep working hard and um have my faith and keep pushing. That's That's about it. >> You know it works though. I mean, the texts come in from the family, from the friends. How do you kind of that noise? >> I mean, um just kind of um take it as what it is as as support, you know what I mean. Um I appreciate them, but at the same time the the work is never done. Um like you like you guys said, this is a a great receiver core. So, anything can happen as far as um as this receiver room. So, each day just try to get better um personally and whatever happens happens. >> Spring football didn't always exist. You know, what kind of opportunity was that that you have felt kind of maybe showcase a little bit more what you're about and get this opportunity here? >> Uh it was great honestly cuz the past couple four years I've been in league but I've been on practice squad. So I'll get elevated every other game and um you know, be back at practice squad. So being in the UFL I got a lot of ops and I was able to just play each game. I mean, we just played 10 games. So just having that that that season with with them was great and had a lot of opportunities to get better. >> And then you said you're you're drowning out the noise but then really had high praise for the special teams stuff. Look back at your last opportunity in Washington you played a ton in those those three games. You know, what what's the background on special teams? What do you like about you know, playing those roles? >> Uh so my whole life I I played DB. I played safety corner. So I kind of always got that physical edge to me that physical side to me. Try to be cuz on teams you got to be physical. So um each each play is just who want to who wanted more. It's a whole lot of effort and just being where you need to be honestly. >> The joke is that DBs are wide receivers that can't catch. Were you a DB that could catch? That's why they didn't >> Yeah, yeah definitely was. >> [laughter] >> Dan brought up your blocking as well as a receiver. What makes a good blocker? >> Uh the will the mentality just going there and then um you know, do what you got to do to get that guy out of there. It's it's it's me or him. So just just going there with that mentality to help my team as much as I can. So when I got a blocking play I'm trying to do what I can for the team anytime I get that.
