Like it would seems like it's carried over so far in camp. Would you say AD Mitchell is clearly their number two wide receiver at this point? >> Absolutely. Yeah, I mean he was the talk of the off season. He's had a solid camp. I think the coaches are excited about him. He he is no doubt the number two receiver. Vertical presence, size, acceleration. You know, I want to see him be a little more consistent on a day-to-day basis, but that's kind of the knock on him the last couple of years is just the consistency. Got the talent, just got to be consistent. >> You know, I wanted to go back to Taysir Mitchell as well and you've been I mean

title: New England Patriots Offensive Assistants Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: Some of our leadership standpoint, last year, very much D'Onta Harris as well. Is it one of the good efforts so far this year? >> I would agree with that. Yeah, I think everybody's had their moments where they felt like it's their time to speak up a little bit. But I also would say that you know the the same tone setters and pace setters from last year, you know, like Matt Collins with his effort and finish, right? And his tenacity in the run game and Braxton Berrios with his willingness to do any role at any time and go running out there as the first sub for whatever position. That's carried over and and even been enhanced with some of the new guys that we've added. And so, you know, I want that room to be their culture. It's not me trying to set a a certain tone. It's how do we put the team first and do anything the team needs and those guys have really embodied that. >> Mike LaFleur talked about this being a just a big week for you guys with six in a row joint practice at the end. I know we hear a lot about the joint practice being these, you know, great examples for preparation. But for your room specifically, what are you looking for in leading into and then in the joint practices? >> Well, I think anytime you're going against someone that doesn't know your offense almost as well as you do, you know, it gives us a chance to, you know, work on some of those route crafts and details where you don't have Gonzo cheating an in route or, you know, somebody calling out one of Drake's signals or something. So, that's always good. But the second piece of it to me is that there are new coverage structures. There's new indicators on defense. And so, our decision-making and play speed really gets tested, you know, from from a different, you know, kind of structure and and field standpoint. So, I'm excited to see our guys handle that. You know, we've kind of taken a one day at a time approach and we got a couple more days against our guys before a New Jersey comes to town. >> I know you do, which is you mentioned Sauce there. You guys got Sauce Gardner last week. You have Quincy Wilson, Cooper DeJean. Like, what's it mean to be able to go up against that level of corner in this setting? >> Oh, it's great. I mean, we're we're so blessed with the work that we get every day against our starting corners and really our whole secondary because, you know, they're they're so talented and uh, you know, I I think they're in the upper echelon of of any of the secondaries that that we'll face this year. But, anytime that you go against somebody else, you want to be able to go against their best, you know, and and see if you are really sturdy against uh, top-level competition. And so, we're excited about the opportunity Sauce last week and and the rest of the secondary, but also Philly coming in with some pretty darn good players and Sauce. >> You talked a lot last year about the unselfish mentality of the group. Do you see that same thing happening this year? And if so, why? >> I do, and I've I've heard even more of it. You know, it uh, it's no secret that we got a a pretty deep room. The way that those guys have approached this training camp where Kayshon might have a good, you know, the the the best day by production standards and then AJ the next day and so on and so forth. You see them celebrating each other just like we did last year and uh, that's my favorite part about coaching those guys. They love each other, they cheer each other on, and not one time have I ever heard someone say, "Well, you know, when am I going to get my uh, >> Obviously, AJ and Romeo both kind of play similar roles to what Kayshon did last year. Is Kayshon a guy who can show some versatility this year by slotting in in multiple different spots? >> Yeah, I think I think you'd be a little careful with what they maybe did in other places and saying that's exactly what they have to be here. Uh, we're looking to get the best two, three, four, shoot, hopefully five receivers on the field, uh, you know, as many times as we can. And so, their job is to go out and execute with whatever route they have, whatever blocking assignment they have, and go do it well, then that gives me the ammo to ask for more of Sauce on the field. >> Obviously, Captain's game grow or kind of evolve in this sub camp here. >> I think uh, much like Pop, he's more and more comfortable with some of the decisions he's being asked to make. So, it helps him play faster and maybe a little bit more comfortable with some defensive recognition, which leads him to some better decisions. Um, I think he's gotten stronger and I think you can see his sturdiness and his uh, route craft and play strength, and that's been really cool to watch as well. Love where Ashton's at. I think that, you know, he put a really hard off season in and worked in his, you know, >> How much has your evaluation of his professionalism with all this noise going on around him? >> It's an example I will use for the rest of my coaching career. The the way that he has just been a pro and shown up every day. I have a great relationship with K'Shawn and and I value that a lot. So, we keep our conversations private, but I will tell you this, he is an absolute joy to coach, and I'm really glad he's here. >> You know, I've experienced that myself as a player. I was a tackle in college and moved inside. It's definitely Now, things happen a lot faster, quicker, you know what I'm saying? So, it's it's a little bit challenging, and I think, you know, James has accepted that, and he's working his butt off to do the best job he can. But, you know, I've no no problem with the effort and how he's competing, and and he is getting better. I mean, everyone's going to be getting better, right? If they're practicing and they're out there doing that, you know, if they're not, then I wouldn't be here talking, you know what I'm saying? It'd be somebody else. >> Hey, sorry to cut you off. >> Last question, guys. Last question. >> When it comes to Jared, just how have you seen him handle transition to center and get back to that guy? >> Yeah, I think it was it was easier for easy for him because he's done it, you know, and that's where he felt comfortable prior to it. I think it was a tougher transition, you know, last year going from being a center in college going to guard. So, I think that's been easier, and like I said before, I think, you know, there's a lot of different things playing, you know, center in the NFL is quite different than, you know, playing center in college, you know, just from the looks and what you have to do from the communication between the volume. So, you know, when there's different things and different looks, they're going to involve different types of techniques, you know, especially when you're very mobile, which all all of us are, you know, at this level. So, there are things that may come up that he might not have experienced before in college. You know, we talk about it, we go over it, and he's he's very steady. That's the one thing about Jared I would say as far as you know, you never see him really you know, too high, he's never really too low. He kind of approaches the job, you know, very well with an understanding and he's a very good communicator. Hey, this doesn't feel right, this doesn't feel good, you know, what can we do to make it better? You know, there's a lot of different ways to do it, so I don't see any issue.

title: Will Campbell, Craig Woodson, DeMario Douglas & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: The the elbow. I'm sure a lot was made of the the brace. What sort of went into that and is it really just sort of nothing? >> Just protecting myself. It's really all there is to it. >> Was there anything that sort of led to it or was it just sort of a precautionary? >> Precautionary. >> So, what were you guys doing inside there with >> Uh just working on some things that uh are going to help us uh in the future with uh some crowd noise. >> Sound accounting >> Yeah, just that type of thing. Yep. >> When in the future do you think? >> When would you guess? When will we have to use crowd noise? Silent week one. So, just trying to get through everything we can to put ourselves in the best position possible. >> How prevalent has that been? I know today was the first time we saw you guys do that, but just understanding Seattle is a loud environment. Is it something that's been frequently talked about in the game? >> I mean, not really. I mean, we're really focusing right now on training camp and you know, this week that you know, that we're coming up. This is a big week for us as a team uh and just focus on that, but anytime that you know, we can work uh towards something that's going to help us in the future, I think is a good opportunity to do that. >> What did you learn against Indy in that joint practice that you could sort of use to help you against Indy? >> Yeah, I I think just getting reps against different guys. They have a very experienced front. A bunch of guys that have played a lot of football. So, you know, getting out there, seeing a different defense from ours, playing against different guys and what we've been going to is always nice uh to get out there and compete and uh it was it was super fun uh going against other people. >> Now you've had some more uh live reps in the padded practices. What's it been like working next to Elijah? >> It's been great. Uh I've really enjoyed it. He's a hell of a player uh and I'm just really excited to you know, keep going and keep building with him. >> You guys have obviously had a ton of reps, so to speak, but will you lobby to play on Saturday? >> Will I >> Will you lobby to play on Saturday? >> That's not my decision, you know, that's a long way away. Tomorrow we got practice. That's really all I'm worried about. We got to have a good practice from start to finish, uh which we didn't do the other day, and uh you know, that's something we got to focus on. Go clean up anything we just messed up and just get ready to go for tomorrow. >> You mentioned you did Bobby 2 get off the weekend update. Are you locked back in for season 2? >> I'm trying like hell to get off of that. Uh but it's not it's not looking like it's going, you know, start that way. So, hopefully I can just maybe do it a couple times and show the next representative of that uh the way to do it, and then we can pass it on. >> Why don't you like it? >> I feel like uh no, I don't mind it. I don't mind it. It's actually fun. Feel like I do a decent job at it. I just don't want to do it every year, basically. I'd like another rookie to do it or just kind of pass it on. >> When it comes to punch timing, we see where you were pretty advanced in that area as a rookie. What do you feel like you've learned now that you have a full season under your belt doing it in the SEC versus doing it with the pros? How do you feel like you've advanced in that >> Yeah, what? Just like and my punching and you said that was what you said? I mean I I think just punch timing is all about reps. I think you know, that's a big thing whenever you come into OTAs, you know, your punch timing is definitely off from where it was, you know, when you come from the season just because, you know, you hadn't been getting those live reps. Uh you know, against a guy moving at you full speed. It's all been off season with bags and things like that. So, I think really just reps and uh you know, working different things with your hands, different ways to shoot them, different ways to show them, and not giving, you know, the edge guy the same look every time, whether that's your set and your punches is just something I'm trying to do. >> Is adding more variety to your set something that you tried to kind of emphasize this off season? >> Yeah, I'm I mean, I think it's kind of, you know, like a pitcher. you know, if you if you know the pitcher's going to throw a fastball every time, more than likely you're going to hit it. Uh so, trying to keep people on their toes and you know, it it's a chess match between a tackle and a edge rusher, you know. They have a plan, we have a plan, and it's who can, you know, disturb the other one's plan, and you know, that's just something I'm trying to do, still trying to you know, work on and still got a long way to go to be where I want to be with it. Uh but just getting out here working it uh and honing in on it every single day is something I've been trying to do. >> Will, how much did working with veterans this off season help you in terms of preparing for this season? >> Yeah, I I think it helped. I I think really the biggest thing was is just getting around those guys that have played a lot of football, but not only played played at a high level, they've won, you know, Super Bowls, they've done everything that, you know, a young aspiring tackle like myself, you know, hopes and plans to do uh with this career. Uh so, I was just, you know, super grateful to, you know, be invited uh by Lane and uh yeah, I mean, it was awesome to just get around those guys, compete, work off, and just really get after it. >> Thank you, Will. >> Yeah, yeah, have a good day. >> Yeah, I mean, me and him talk every day. We talk uh you know, just about things we're seeing, uh stuff outside of ball. I mean, we're we're building a good connection and it's going to keep on improving, so uh I'm excited to keep on working with him. >> One of the things that Del told us a couple weeks ago was that he had a meeting with you guys and stressed the need for takeaways. >> Yeah. >> And then, first preseason game, it's not the only reason, but it's not coincidental that >> Mhm. >> practice out here. >> Is that a coincidence I'm guessing? Is that the best way to ask it is that a coincidence or what do you How do you see that? >> I mean, you know, I don't know if that's a you know, a coincidence of you know, something that he said and it's happening, but I mean at the end of the day that's that's what we got to do on defense create takeaways and we did that in the game and uh the guys that played man they did a good job of doing that and that helps us win games. So, we just got to keep going with that. >> Last question for Kevin. How have you seen his leadership? Mike has praised his leadership in conversation with that. How have you seen his leadership manifest itself in the locker room and on the field? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, he has a has a voice that's really uh empowering when it comes to just you know, some of the things that he's able to preach to us as a DB group and um even to the coaches as well. So, I think that when when he speaks people listen and um that's just you know, something that you don't get with you know, a lot of players. So, it's good to have that leadership in the room and I think that's just going to help us. >> What did you take away from the joint practice with Indy that you can sort of help you against Philly? >> Yeah, I mean that was good work. Uh it's good to you know, compete against somebody else other than your own team. Uh just see a couple things on you know, how people move and stuff like that and how you can play it. Uh we learned a lot from the joint practice and uh it's going to be the same thing with Philly. >> It's your comfortability factor. How comfortable were you last year at this point? >> Yeah, very comfortable. I mean, at this point I know the playbook. Uh I have the experience of playing and now it's just you know, going to make plays and not second guessing and uh just trusting what I see. >> What have you seen from John Johnson that has struck our perspective this >> That's the summer practices as well. >> Man, John has always made plays like it's crazy we just watched his college tape and we didn't even know he went crazy like that. It was man, he he makes plays, he know how to be around the ball and uh he keeps keeps improving and uh you know, that's that's cool to see and just cool to experience. So, I you know, I'm proud of him and I just hope if keeps it up. >> Mike said yesterday that there were times last year where they had to dial John back in practice cuz he'd go too hard. >> What do you remember about him as a rookie last year just kind of day-to-day? >> Yeah, I remember I think his first practice here, he got a pick in practice and I was like, "Damn, like who is this dude?" But I mean, yeah, John goes hard. He gives good looks. And he's got us going to be attentive in the classroom and yeah, I mean, he just keeps improving and he's doing his thing right now. So. Appreciate y'all. >> Thanks. Thank you. >> What's up? How you doing? >> Good, Mike. >> I know it's not your job to coach, but I just any big differences between you and Will? Like you had a a leap your rookie year to year two. >> Uh-huh. Um just more leadership, you know, he's a young guy, but going to his second year, he's played a lot, seen a lot. So, just encouraging him and Moses as well and all the tackles and all the coaches, just bringing him along and just putting him in that on that pedestal and you know, he's working up to that and you know, that's the type of work that we look for. >> Do you want him to keep the weekend update job? >> Yeah, I would like that. I would like that, yeah, yeah. Bring a smile to my face. >> Mike, you guys are going to have a lot of reps this week, obviously, but do you feel like you I guess not necessarily should, but do you want to play on Saturday? Yeah, any any ball is, you know, that's my job, you know, I like playing football. So, you know, any any any any game I would like to play. It's a good competition, of course, so you know, I'm looking forward to that. >> Mike, just curious, a lot of people made of that new virtual room in the practice facilities. How have you guys in the offensive line line room been able to use that? >> Yeah, we've used it. It's always nice in between, you know, going from meeting and sitting in the meeting room to getting up, doing it virtually, going through the plays, looking at defenses and working through those plays virtually or I guess in person, doing them in person like you would on a football field versus just watching a film in the classroom. >> How was Caleb done to this point in the summer? >> Caleb done good. He's really Now he's played a lot of a lot of roles. Played wore a lot of hats. So I think he's done a good job of that. I think day day in and day out he's done well just uh uh managing, you know, asks and and wants and needs and all that. But he's he's playing well and he's really grown up. >> One of the things that that he's talked about is that Morgan has said, "Look, don't bring a whole laundry list of stuff to the field >> every day. Just like focus on one thing." >> Can you remember that development and maybe you kind of looked up to to Caleb to kind of you know follow that path? >> As far as doing that? >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, he has. You know, we all of us have things to work on each day. But for Caleb, like I said, just juggling many positions or many Now whether it's left or right, doing certain things or knowing what to do on certain plays and stuff like that. He's brought that to the field and he's done a good job of that. >> Mike, how do you think going inside working on the silent count and stuff? How do you think that went today? >> Yeah, I think that went well. This is our second or third time doing it. Think it'll work well. It's just been one of those things that works well for away games and working on the silent count and just being in those uncomfortable situations. >> You guys didn't do that a ton last year, did you? >> Not as far as in the bubble, but we did we did silent count. We did working on like away games and stuff like that and working on our cadence and stuff like that. But just being more more ahead of it this year around. >> What's the biggest challenge there other than not having dealing with the noise? What's the biggest challenge >> for you guys? >> It's really just communication. You know, the picture changes, the defense changes. You know, just being able to talk to the guy to the left and right and just hearing the calls, whatever Drake is saying or if the play is changing, you know, hearing like a danger call from the left side knowing that we're going to get slant or pressure from the right side or something like that. When um you know, just I think it all helps and it ties it all together. >> Mike, you've played a lot of football. You've done it at a high level. How do you continue to keep yourself challenged and engaged? Because I can assume that doing this every year can be Um it's really the guys that's in the room, you know, I look at the guys around me, whether it's Jerry, ABT, Will, Mo. You know, I look at them, seeing how their work ethic are and just seeing what they put on tape, put on film. So, you know, it really just encourages me myself as well just to do the same and you know, be as good as they are. >> Two more? >> You said who? Sorry. Yep, yep. >> I've seen you play some guard and tackle. >> Are you able to help with all that transition? >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. James has been good. Um you know, at tackle he's been he's been good. On our inside he's a he's an athletic, you know, player overall, but um just on the inside it does does him well just to be able to have that play speed and have that play strength, you know, he doesn't really have to move too much, but you know, if he does, he has that athleticism to catch up or, you know, if he has to make up a block or something like that. But um I think James has done well. He's taking all the coaching uh going from outside to inside or uh tackle to guard and then um you know, he's came through and worked every day at it. So, I I I think I'm happy about James. >> Mike, and just finally, how much does your experience in Josh's system >> help you help the new guys, whether it be Elijah >> or Caleb >> transitioning into the new system? >> Yeah, for sure. I think it helps. I mean, we're we're all still learning the system or, you know, in the line now. Um you know, I I I I think it just helps uh with the communication, you know, whether there's something that that we ran a couple years ago and you know, whatever it's called now and stuff like that. Uh just verbalizing that and really just being in the system and uh kind of explaining, talking to the guys and just, you know, whether there's certain looks or certain blitzes or whether there's squeeze look or something like that where we is just this certain look that we have to block it this way, something like that. I think it helps uh you know, being in the system, yeah. Sure. Thank you. How you doing? >> Good. Yourself? >> Doing good. >> With uh let's start with the importance maybe of this week for you guys, when it comes to what you'd like to accomplish. >> Um just getting better every day, honing in more on our craft. Um being very focused on what's being asked of us and being very focused on the play calls. >> What did joint practices, two joint practices do for you guys? >> Um it's the same as every day. It just adds another level of competition to it with another opponent coming in. So, you know, you got a fresh guy coming in who doesn't know your your your moves as much. So, it's cool to get a different feel. >> Thought on your craft and what you're doing. I see a lot a lot of spending a lot of time continuing with Mike Smith. Is that mental? What kind of things are you talking about with him? >> Um my alignment, my footwork, my hand placement, my timing of my hands, um how I want to approach a guy who soft sets compared to a hard setter. Um a bunch of different things like >> How much have you grown with that over the years? >> Uh I mean, it always gotten better and better, you know, in the beginning stages you don't really see or you can't really tell cuz you're just trying to go so fast and so hard. But now, I've kind of like trained my mind to slow down and to be able to see things and I got a good feel of guys' body position now. Been a year eight. >> Have you you played obviously, you know, Vrabel, you know the staff. >> What are some similarities schematically? Have you been able to just walk right in and adjust to this scheme or have you had to pick up some new things? >> Uh no, for the most part I I kind of just came in and kind of knowing what to expect because I've been in a system for a while. So, I mean, I mentioned before like it's pretty much the same, but like there's a couple like verbages that are different, but um it's it's the same. Yeah, I left yesterday. Yeah, I'm fine. I'm all good. Uh I got a I got a cut on my finger and I had to get Yeah, I had to go inside, you know. No, that's not what happened. >> [laughter] >> On the finger? That's smart. Yeah, I I I had to go tie my shoe in the in the training room real quick. So, they got to just Yeah. Yeah, I'm fine. Yeah, I'm all good. >> What do you make of the uh some of the guys in your room, the younger players pushing for playing time? Obviously, Gabe is uh had to hit the ground running here. >> Mhm. Um I think they're all in their own way trying to do their best job of making sure they're prepared for the game. Um they they definitely saw the speed of the game coming this uh this past Thursday. Uh it wasn't as sweet as as practice. You know, cut practice get a little comfortable. That fan and uh that fan environment and that stage environment kind of brings more out of people. And uh some of the guys were, you know, at the start were kind of head in the clouds, but they kind of they kind of calmed down and got used to the the the game. And I I thought they progressed and got better as the game went on. >> You were asked about the joint practices. They have two tackles who are considered One of them is considered the the best right tackle, and the left tackle is pretty damn good. >> Do you use this as a bit of a measuring stick for you, or you know, hey, like I'm pacing myself. I know exactly where I'm supposed to be and >> Nah, I mean, there's there's no there's no fear in me at all with with things like that. I don't give a a damn if it was the the best tackle ever to play football. Like I mean, it is what it is. I'm I'm going out there to to to show what I can do for myself and for this team. Like, you know, whether I do good or do bad, you know, it won't it won't measure up to how I feel about myself and how I feel about how I've done this camp, but I I obviously want to go out there and and kick some >> All right, last one. Just mean, how sharp do you feel as far as getting ready for what you need to ultimately get ready for as you progress here day-to-day? >> Um I'm feeling solid right now. I can always be sharper. I can always be more clean. I mean, this is this is a game where I'm always looking for imperfections, and I'm always trying to be better each and every day. So, uh the more the more I'm out there sharpening my tools, the better I am, whether that's uh the mental aspect or the physical aspect. >> All right, thanks you. >> Thank you. >> Pomphrey, just some thoughts on how it's gone for you this camp so far. Obviously, you know, you've come in and you're now in another year in the system. >> How have you been acclimating to playing in your second year in Josh McDaniels' offense? And how's camp gone for you? >> Yeah, I've been feeling good, you know, just you know, out there playing with confidence. Like I say, you know, that first year you out there, you really trying to learn it before you get gain that confidence. Then gain that confidence took probably closer to the end of the year. So, I mean, just to start off with that confidence is amazing and grow. It's going to help me grow. >> How's the competition been? >> Oh, it's been good. You know, our room is very stacked, you know, competition is what's going to help us be a great room, you know, if we don't see that competition, man, I I don't believe we should be in this room, you know, that that competition is what's is what's going to make us >> You said you felt night and day coming into Josh's offense. Has that progress continued for you comfort-wise? >> Oh, yeah, most definitely. I wouldn't say, I mean, I'm learning still as I go, but just to know like the basics, I would say, you know, I go out there with confidence and then line up quick, you know, line up quick and just, you know, read the defense. I go out there read the defense and know what I need to do. >> Talking to the coach down there and said, you know, obviously you didn't didn't start last year. Played a little bit less than other receivers. Asked him about a change about this year. He said that part of it was the makeup of the room. >> How do you think the makeup of the room might help you this year? it's going to push me, you know, feel like I I got competition too, you know, every position, every you know, in receiver room position, I feel like we we got competition. So, can't let my foot off the gas, you know, feel like everybody in our room can play every position. So, anything can change, so, you know, I feel like I just got to keep my foot on the gas and that's going to even help the people behind me and in front of me. >> How does a guy like Easton push you? >> Mhm. Oh, man, that's man, I I I that guy, you know, uh just his his work ethic, you know, um for me, when I came in, I seen, you know, Pep, you know, really work hard, you know, my first year. I watched him. That was the first person I seen really work hard like from practice and game and look the same. You so, you know, um it was hard to find somebody like that, you know, who practice just like that, you know, just like me and just to watch Cheers, man, he he he practice just like it's a game, you know, and man, that's that's great competition. I always learned that the practice got to be like the game so the game could be easy. And I feel like my guys is pushing me to be better also. >> And that was Jabrill Peppers? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> For you getting a little work with silent counts in the bubble? >> Oh, yeah, just a little loud just for loud noises. >> Does it Does it help to go through that kind of stuff like when you show up in Seattle week one, you know, you >> it'll be kind of second nature, maybe? >> Yeah, you know, away games is always like that, you know, away games would be loud. So, just learn that now is just going to help us throughout the season. >> Pop, how do you feel you were talking about like they want you to paint don't necessarily paint by numbers, do a little bit of your own thing and your flavor on it. Todd was saying you got, you know, there you want to do that, but then you also got to make sure that it's still within the framework. How do you feel like that process is going for you? >> Man, it's going good, you know, TD lets us, you know, be a little creative, you know, add your little spice to it. You don't want to do what is on the piece of paper, you know, cuz you going to have a different look on defenses. Going to be a different look from different teams. So, you know, TD job do be like, "Hey, add your spice to it, you know, give it some time, you know, do what you do and go out there and play free." And that's why I said play with confidence, you know, that that's helping me play with more confidence. >> What kind of spices do you like? >> Man, hot spices. >> Yeah, honestly, whatever my grandma cook. >> Also, grandma said that's it. >> Yeah, that Yeah, she the boss. Yeah. >> How do you feel AJ and tomorrow's personality wise change the the fiber of the wide receiver room. >> Oh man, AJ he pretty funny, you know, pretty funny guy. You you wouldn't expect it cuz you know, bro huge. But man, pretty funny guy and definitely have a lot of knowledge of the game. So definitely pick his brain. And Rome, man, he got great knowledge, too. And just to see what he does is amazing on and off the field. Very quiet dude, but if you talk to him, very funny dude. So yeah, I get to pick his brain. Just you know, try to make him laugh. You know, he he might not laugh, but he a fun he is a funny cat. >> Marvin, you feeling you find more roles? >> Last one. >> On the field, but obviously as a slot guy, we're used to seeing you catch a lot of crossing routes. It looks like in this camp you've been at the other layers as well. Do you feel like you've been downfield a little bit more this summer than >> Uh yeah, I probably have probably caught some. I mean, last year I had them, but probably didn't catch them get to catch them. So it's been a blessing. You know, just to you know, be a threat up down the field and you know, close. So I feel like you know, shout out to the coach. >> All right, thanks, Marvin. >> Yep, thank you. >> How you doing? >> I'm good. I'm good. How y'all doing? >> Good. Good. >> What's the process like for you getting back into the game last Thursday night? >> Uh you know, I take it one day at a time. You know, uh the first preseason game, it was just you know, I was just lucky to be back playing football, you know, with an organization as good as this one. And you know, I was just excited to be out there. You know, I was just wanting to have fun, you know, and uh just glad to be back. >> Were you swimming a little bit in the playbook, trying to crash and learn some things? >> I mean, a little bit, but my coach Tony Dukes, he he do a good job you know, explaining different stuff and like at a level that I can, you know, take take in. And uh, you know, so it wasn't too bad, but uh, I definitely been studying the past past couple days. >> What's Tony conveyed just about the state of the room and what it'll take to win the job here on the 53? >> You know, we all we we is a a one unit, uh, one if one man can do it, we all can do it, you know, and then that's just our mindset and uh, you know, one man's success is everybody's success in the room. So, we just take that as take that and run with it. >> How nice is it to reunite with Mike Vrabel? >> Man, it's nice, man. That's That's That's my guy for sure, you know, we definitely got history and uh, you know, I'm excited to be back, you know, I know the the mindset he got and uh, you know, I'm I'm going to bring it here and you know, we going to be going to be fine. >> How would you just describe your overall game? >> My overall game? I feel like I'm a physical back, but I feel like I can I can move well, you know, I got different you know, I got a different tools in my tool bag. I feel like I, you know, I can bring to the table, so. >> What have your interactions with Josh McDaniels been like and what are your thoughts on on his offense as you start digging into it? >> No, he's been he's been good. I definitely I definitely like Josh a lot, you know, he knows he knows what he's talking about and uh, I feel like he going to bring this whole offense together and uh, you know, we going to do we going to it's going to be a good year this year. >> Are there any former Patriots running backs that maybe you studied, you know, in the college or as you got in the NFL? >> Uh, not too many, but uh, you know, I'm still learning about, you know, the Patriots history and all that, but uh, I'm going to go back and find some some, you know, just study the game and stuff like that, so. >> What have you seen from Drake Maye so far? It hasn't been that long, but what have you seen from him? >> Yeah, it hasn't been too long, but uh, I love his game, you know, just just past couple days I've been here, he he's he's he's a he's a really good football player. Let me say that and uh, you know, it's going to be exciting this year. I feel like he going to he going to put up some big numbers and you know, we going to we He's to be he's going to be he's going to be fun to watch. >> What's your uh experience level been like on special teams for your career? >> Man, I always feel like I always I bring a good um good attributes to special teams, you know. Uh I just always did it in college, you know, stuff like that. So, it just always was built in me and I feel like any way I can get on the field, I'm going to I'm going to do it and uh do the best of my ability. So, you know. >> I got some uh kick return experience and catching punts and kicks in college. Just how do you feel like you've adjusted to the new the new format? >> Yeah, the new format is definitely different, but I mean, it is what it is, you know. It's That's the new format and you know, I feel like I can like I said, any any way I can get on the field, I'm going to do it and uh and try my best, you know, whatever it is. So, >> Is there anything you learned about yourself as a player or as a person the last few weeks where you were weren't signed? Is that something that sort of reflected on yourself? What What did you learn about yourself in >> Uh you know, just um don't take nothing for granted. You know, uh you know, I love being out here with a team, with a family. And you know, and uh it just you know, just have long days, you know, not not being with your family brotherhood and stuff like that. So, you know, just don't take nothing for granted and uh just come out here every each every and each day and just be thankful, you know, you uh have a team and a family like this. So, >> Thank you. Appreciate y'all. Thank you. Thank you.

title: Josh McDaniels: "It's an Enjoyable Time to be a Coach." | Patriots Press Conference
text: What do you get from joint practices? >> Uh different different atmosphere, different anxiety, different adrenaline, uh different sense of urgency. Um you know, you're practicing against guys that you're not familiar with. Um it's a great change of pace for us. We'll see a different scheme. Saw one last week. We'll see another one this week. Um you know, and it's just it's a great opportunity for us to test our rules, test what we know. uh compete against another um group of players uh in this case obviously one of the best teams in the National Football League this week. So um those are exciting. We learn a lot. Uh hopefully the work is great for both sides. We keep each other off the ground as much as we can and and stay healthy. So um I do I do five or six of them if they let if they let us. You talked a lot about, you know, the players too about how different mini camp was this year because of the advancement in year two under you. How is training camp different? How is it different for Drake in in your relationship? Are you talking more about plays you like, plays you don't like? What kind of things? >> Yeah, there's less there's less uh explaining that the foundation of what we do and how we do it and more of trying to get really good at it, I think, this year. So, um, you know, it's it's when you have this many guys in camp, um, they're all at different places. So, each quarterback's at a different place, each player in in the other position rooms are at different places. So, you're trying to teach kind of globally to the unit, but also, uh, drill down so that each each guy on the offense gets what he needs from the coaches. So, um, it's it's a it's a great time. It's an enjoyable time to be a coach because you have a lot of uh different things that you have to tackle at the same time. Um, but you know, certainly I think the foundation of what we try to do, I think we understand and now it's trying to, you know, get as good as we can at it before the end of camp. >> Josh, have you seen Drake improve in terms of handling the pressure looks and blitzes and stuff like that pre- snap? And how much of an emphasis has that been after, you know, the Super Bowl and things like that? >> Um, yeah, I mean, he's certainly he's made progress in every area. Um, you know, I think I think we would continue to hope hope to see that as we go forward. Um, you know, he works his butt off to try to um get really good at at every aspect of playing the position. That's a that's a unique situation in and of itself because it's a challenge based on what type of pressures you're seeing or what the defense presents to you. So, um, we see it every day from our defense. Different looks, different things. Uh it's a great opportunity for us to learn and grow. Um he's certainly embraced that. Um I also think that's a that's a unit thing. You know, there's a lot of guys >> when you're talking about handling those types of situations well. It's not a oneman show, you know. So, uh Drake certainly has to do his part, but it's 111th of the group and and we're going to need everybody else to to do their part, too. So, I think our unit has embraced that. Um, you know, certainly a challenge against our group on defense and, uh, we'll continue to get better at it, I hope, as we finish training camp here. >> Josh, I know in the offseason >> get a gauge on where the winning game is. Is it hard to get a gauge on the winning game during this part of training camp where you start to feel like, hey, this is what this is what? It's it's it's always a little difficult to gauge this because, you know, you don't tackle the runner, which people sometimes forget like the runner's pretty big part of the running game, you know what I mean? And getting them onto the ground is is is in and of itself not an easy thing to do. So, uh, we got some good backs. Um, they do things with the ball in their hands. And I know sometimes it looks like maybe the play was, you know, a three or four yard run, but it might not have been. it might have been bigger than that. So, um, the runner plays a role. I think all the other aspects of taking care of each other. Um, you know, we're not really trying to, you know, put people on the ground. We're certainly not cutting on the backside. You know, it was, it was good to see us the other night in a game, get a couple, you know, you get an opportunity to cut somebody, uh, because it's, you know, it's an actual football game. So, um, there's certain things you have to kind of, you know, uh, continue to coach and work on without seeing them. Um, but honestly, you never really know. You know, you get to the regular season and then uh I think that the last 10 years here, maybe even longer, has become one of the the great challenges uh for coaches is the running game needs to be continued uh you know, continued work in progress as we enter the regular season, September, October. And I thought last year we made progress as the season went on and uh I don't see this year being any different. Josh, I know in the offseason, you know, you review the entire season you just had and to inform your changes, right? What you want to do this year. How much did the last two games though that you guys play informed the changes either schematically or teaching that that you made? >> You're talking about last season. >> Yeah. Yeah. Um, I mean, not it didn't change what we what we do in terms of foundationally or the way we um, you know, put our system in or anything like that, but look, the the best teams you play are in the postseason. There's no question about that. So, um, I I have always thought when you get there, it's the best coaches, it's the best players, and they're playing the best and coaching the best at the right time of the year. So, there's no greater challenge that that that we face. So, um I I think we learned a lot. Um I think we've we've grown. Uh how much so we'll find out soon enough. Um but uh those are great lessons and you know we we kind of had that same mentality all year last year. Either you won or you learned and so you know uh unfortunately the the you know the the last so so many games weren't necessarily our finest offensively but um a lot of lessons to be learned, a lot of things to be gained. How much uh does it help you uh when you have so many tall receivers who go up and get it uh particularly in the red zone? >> Pop would be offended by that. [laughter] Um no um look the you know that's uh certainly a benefit um when you have an opportunity to uh to do that where somebody's um you know god-given height, weight, speed, whatever it might be uh size uh can help you uh in those types of areas you know whether it be third down or in a red area. Um, we're trying, Karen. We're trying to, you know, to to use all the different things we have, whether that's quickness by some people, speed, size, um, you know, our personnel, you know, and and this is probably the norm. Uh, your personnel has different strengths and weaknesses. And so, um, hopefully we're putting the guys that have those traits in the right positions to have a chance to be successful, make an impact because there's no greater, uh, you know, part of the field for us, you know, to focus on and try to improve than there. >> Josh, what makes, uh, what makes Romeo Dodd so effective in the low red zone area? When you watch him last year, he >> Yeah, >> he did a lot of good work in that area of the field. What do you think makes him so effective? >> Rome's doing a great job of of really a lot of things right now. Um he's got a great attitude approach. He works extremely hard at it. Um I think Romeo wants to be good at all aspects of the position of receiver and Todd's doing a tremendous job of coaching him. Um he's bought into the things we do. Um and you can just see I think confidence um and his ability now that he knows exactly what it is we do. um in all areas of the field. Uh Rome is starting to make more plays and more plays and more plays, you know, and so the relationship between a quarterback and a receiver is, you know, is is a is a significant one in terms of body language and trust and understanding what the other one is looking for and how they're going to do things. And I think our group is really growing in that area and Romeo's certainly a big part of that. Josh, it's kind of a a broad question, but I'm curious, you know, as you've studied defense the last couple of years, how have the tools to gain information pre- snap and recoverage changed based on how defenses have kind of evolved with their disguise? >> That's a good question. Um, thank you. >> Yeah, we got a lot of them this morning. um they've definitely tried to evolve um in terms of hiding information. Um I don't think that's a brand new thing. I think that there's different ways people are trying to do it now. Uh some of that has to do with the personnel on the field allowing them to do that. Whether they play a lot more nickel to all groupings than they do base or they play with safeties that are a little smaller, they're really converted corners playing in the secondary back deep, you know, what have you. so that they can drop down and cover and they don't necessarily have to, you know, match bodies all the time. So, um, you know, there's pros and cons to all that. Um, I think there's an adaptation and and evolution every year for us offensively based on what we see the league doing and how we see it changing. Um, this year will be no different, you know. So, uh, the good thing about football is is whatever they do, you know, you always have an opportunity to do something to counter it. Um, and that's the the great part about coaching is there's a there's a there's a fun element of back and forth as we go. So, I'm excited to see kind of, you know, the things we're doing. Um, you know, what what other teams are going to present to us this year in that regard. Uh, but it's certainly a topic and it's definitely something that is evolving and changing. >> Thanks, Josh. Other take.

title: John Harbaugh: ‘The picture starts to clear up a little more after the first game’ | New York Giants
text: So, I guess when you look back at the tape yesterday, did anything kind of just stand out from the game that caught your eye? >> Yeah, lots of things. I mean, you know, talking about to 200 plays. Uh there's a lot of good a lot of good things a lot of things to correct. Uh all across the board it'd be hard to pinpoint any one thing for sure, but I would say the effort if I just generally speaking if there's one thing it would be more general would be just the effort. Uh the attitude Uh you know, the determination to try to do well. That was out there for sure. Uh so, I was happy with that and it was a good first step. We learned a lot. And uh we'll have a lot of a lot of corrections a lot of encouragement to make tomorrow and through the week for sure and hopefully we can make a lot of progress to next week. >> And then last thing for me, did you um with the way the game was called with the first team offense, you guys obviously wanted to establish the run run the ball more. Um and you guys had a nine runs to five passes. Were you pleased with just kind of how that first team offense how the plays were executed and the way that game was called for at least for them trying to run the ball? >> some of it. It wasn't anything that that to really evaluate as far as the way it was called. It wasn't really part of our plan to to game plan in any way. We just wanted to come out and see how we blocked. You know, see if we could execute. I thought we did a good job of you know, getting subs on and off the field. I thought the sideline communication with the players coaches uh coaches to the box all those kind of things. Operation was really good. We didn't have really any issues with subs. We didn't have any issues with clock. Didn't have any really issues with formation. You know, wrong formations things like that or motions all that stuff was good. Uh that that's that's uh underestimated. You know, it's easy to say, oh you know, that should be expected, but look around the league it's it's not. So, I thought all that was really good. Uh our you know, the things that we've got to continue to improve on and why we just called so many basic plays was because you've got to be able to block your plays against whatever look they give you. We had a lot of a lot of different looks from the Vikings. We had a lot of a lot of a lot of run pressures. They gave us a lot of run blitzes they gave us and things like that. You know, we would be schemed up for those things in a real game, but let's just try to block that stuff and see how we do. And that way we can kind of see how our rules are and see how our guys understand it. We learned a lot and probably, you know, three or four or five even of of the plays that that weren't good in the run game, you know, were things that we can easily correct, but it'll be great to see, you know, and then and then when game plan time comes around game plan a little bit more. So, not really looking at the play calling or the game planning as much as we are kind of how we operated and learn where we're at execution-wise. >> Thank you. >> Jordan Renon. >> Hey John, what's going on? >> Hey, doing good. >> Um I'm curious, how important is running backs pass blocking for you and I know some coaches are like, we don't we'll deal we don't we work with our players strengths. Like, is it a non-negotiable for you? Are you able to work around that if that's something with a running back? Where where do you stand on that? >> Well, it's always just give and take. It's always upside downside, you know, uh you going to if you if you're back if you're going to be a passing down back, you got to be great at it. If you're going to be on the field on third down or second and long, you know, with so-called pass downs, you have to be a great pass protection guy because you're going to be throwing the ball a lot, you know, so that'll be a requirement. If you're if you're not that, if you're if you're going to be more of a first down or run down type of guy, play action type guy in that offense, you don't have to be as much of a pass protector cuz you're not in those drop back passing protection modes as much, so uh that's that's it. That's where roles come in. That's where you find guys who are role players that'll you know, they're they're they're in the game say as on maybe third down more than they are on first and second down things like that, so that's kind of how that works. >> And I I know if you heard, you saw Jackson said afterwards he was puzzled by the idea that he, you know, keeps getting called back to the blue tent. I'm curious when you What do you think of that and what did you think when you went back and looked at that? >> Yeah, uh I'm sure it's frustrating, you know, I mean, he was he got the I guess he may maybe got the wind knocked out of him a little bit, but I you know, I I'm not going to be critical of the league, you know, that's or whoever is doing that upstairs. I mean, they they do their job and they they want to protect the players. I'm sure there's I'm sure history or whatever they might remember, maybe that comes into play. I don't know if a similar situation another quarterback would have been called in the tent or not. There's no way for us to know that, so uh just nothing we can worry about. I saw Jackson's comments, it doesn't sound like he's too worried about it, so we'll just keep playing football and and we'll just try to do a better job of protecting him and there's no way he should have been hit there. I mean, it just shouldn't have happened. That was a basic protection. Should have been protected and uh and uh we expect him to be in that situation to be protected in the future. I mean, it's not like he's going to be never hit, never tackled, never sacked, uh but it shouldn't have been in that one. It shouldn't have been that easy to get to him. >> Dan Duggan. >> Hey John, uh curious at the end of the game, why not attempt the uh 62-yard field goal? >> Was it 62? Was that what it would have been? Where was the ball at? What yard line? >> 44, wasn't it? >> 44, was it? I don't know. I can't I can't remember exactly, but no, we thought it was too far into the wind there a little bit. So, that's why. >> And then just on like those types of decisions, challenge, um you know, this is your first game here. I'm just Who's in the headset with you? Like, who's advising you on um game management? >> Ty Siam, the guy that did it like here last year. He did a good job. He did a good job. I I was happy with it. Yeah, I thought we did I thought we did well. I thought the I thought the challenge early was the right challenge. I mean, the ball I thought the ball moved. His hands were on the side, hit the ground, ball moved out of his control. To me, they didn't turn it over probably cuz of the shadowing on the replay. You couldn't really see it probably that clearly. You looked at it for a long time. But I thought ball moved. Good challenge on a, you know, a long third down like that would have got us would have got us off the field. Uh what other ones you want to talk about? >> No, I just been operational cuz we, you know, it's your first game here. I didn't know it was Ty or if there's more people on there. It's just Ty. Like I just didn't know how you how you operating. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, it was that. But I'm I'm talking to Chris Horton about the field goal We both felt like that was just a little long to be realistic on. But we wanted to kick it. I mean, I promise you we wanted to get him out there to try one. So uh it just seemed a little too far. Maybe we would have knocked it through. >> Got you. Thanks. >> Art Stapleton. >> yeah, and the other thing is the other thing is is like we got a really good chance to get the ball back there. I mean, there's over 2 minutes left. You know, we got three timeouts I think we had. So uh you know, if we basically make a tackle, we're getting the ball back there to go kick the same field goal. So it wasn't I don't think it was the wrong thing to do at all. But you put them in You miss it. Now they're in range to they get they get 10 yd and they kick the field goal or put it out of reach, you know. So it wasn't the wrong thing to do. >> Hey John, how's it going? >> Hey, good. Good, Art. >> Um I know a lot was made obviously and rightfully so about Malakai and the touchdown and and what he was able to do on that play with Jackson. Uh I it we knew he was going to be able to uh be a part of your run game with his blocking ability. I'm just curious, he kind of enjoyed talking about the one play he had on uh punt coverage running down the field late in the third quarter. Uh I know it got nullified by a penalty, but making a tackle. Uh I guess if you if you look up what what a wide receiver as a rookie needs to do to impress John Harbaugh, I would imagine he checked those boxes last night. >> Yeah, I thought he played all around really well, you know, I mean, he did do some things on special teams, which is which was cool to see. Uh he he practices that every day really well. Uh he's blocked exceptionally well in the run game uh as a wide receiver in some of those insert blocks and going to get safeties and things like that. Tremendous. Thought he ran his routes really well, even when he didn't get the ball, the routes were run correctly, right depths, uh right amount of steps, right splits. All those things that make so much difference that really honestly we need to clean up across the board to give up, you know, to give our present better pictures for our quarterbacks. So, uh he did all those things really well. He he didn't play like a rookie out there. title: Todd Bowles on Zac Robinson’s First Action as Play-caller | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: If you have any questions, please raise your hand. All right, first question will go to Scott Reynolds. >> Hey coach, congrats on the win. Last night was your first game action with Zach Robinson, your new offensive coordinator. What did you learn about his play calling, his sideline operation from last night? >> I don't think I learned too much. I mean, it's been pretty clean like that since practice, since we started in OTAs and mini camp and it carried over to training camp and it was more of that on the sideline. Thought the communication was great, the understanding of the guys were great. So, you know, I thought it went well. >> Dean Patterson was a player that that got a lot of targets early. What have you seen about him and and didn't have any plays down the field, but but what are your thoughts on how he performed >> He didn't have any plays down the field, but he did make one big catch on a fourth for a short gain right there. He's been coming along, he's a very talented guy, you can see that. He needs more time, a little time to develop from a mental standpoint, from getting the scheme down, but you can tell he's a talented guy and you know, I'm looking forward to these last two preseason games to see where he goes. >> Sorry. >> Thank you. >> Evan Winter, if you have questions, please raise your hand. >> Morning coach, hope you're doing well. >> All right. >> Obviously, y'all sat pretty much all the starters yesterday. I do find it interesting though with Ruben Bain, since you've been head coach, the first pick of the draft has played in the first preseason game outside of Calijah Kancey because he was hurt, obviously. So, is that more of a reflection on Bain and what he's shown throughout training camp and preseason so far? >> And we've seen a lot in preseason and we've seen a lot in practices as well. He got a lot of work in the practice part of it against their number ones and and I was sitting all of them, he wasn't going to get anything out of that game by playing six to eight plays, you know. We'll We'll put all of them out there next week and they'll get a trial run that way. But, we we're satisfied with everything we seen in him. >> And then uh just wanted to get your overall thoughts on the inside linebackers and how they played last night. >> Lot of depth. Still going through the tape. I really thought Fordham uh stepped up and made some plays, you know. He's been getting better week by week. Obviously, Traill has been solid and the rest of the guys I thought Bullet did a good job as well. Still sorting through the tape out for everybody else. >> Thanks. We'll go to Scott Reynolds. >> I can't hear you, Scott. >> Yeah, coach, when you when you go through the tape, obviously, sometimes your better players don't necessarily show up in the stat sheet. Maybe along the defensive line where they're doing some of the dirty work, but who are some of the players that that impressed you last night that maybe didn't garner some headlines such as Carnes and Elijah Roberts, etc. >> I'm still sorting through the tape, Scott. I could tell you I'm about a quarter of the way through, kind of in the second quarter that way. I know they played tough. Still got to figure that out as to who played well down there and where they're supposed to be. I know Elijah Roberts flashed early. He's been having a very good camp in the run game and the pass game and he's one of our best pass rushers which we'll count on, so I saw him flash early. >> And Jack Pyburn, what can you tell us about the camp that he said he did kind of come on the scene last night with a couple of big plays and a couple of sacks for you. >> He did a heck of a job last night. He showed up with the lights on. Uh he's a solid player. He doesn't get much run with all the other guys playing, you know. You got Bang there and Muhammad there and Yaya as well as David Walking and all those other guys there. You don't hear about them much, but he got a chance to play last night and he showed everybody who he was. He's a hard worker. He comes off the ball hard and, you know, you look forward to seeing more how he put his whole game together last night. >> We'll go to Greg Auman. >> Hey Todd, I know obviously you you held out the key players on offense and defense. It looked like you might have done the same thing on teams as well with guys like Hayes and Roseboom. Just wanted to ask you if they're healthy and you just held them out just to make sure you had kind of your key people on special teams held out as well. >> No, they were banged up a little bit so they didn't play. They would have played. >> When you in terms of any injuries in game, are there guys that that took on injuries? It looked like you were able to get through it pretty cleanly. >> Uh still waiting for the training to get a report. They are checking at 11:00 this morning. I have more for you then, but I didn't hear anything, but you know, usually that's not a good sign, so hopefully that's a good sign today. >> Okay, thank you. >> We'll go to Evan Winter. If any media have questions, please raise your hand. >> Hey coach, it looked like David Walker, especially there in the beginning, was getting double-teamed almost every single play. I just wanted to kind of get your thoughts on his performance and just how much the league is starting to catch on potentially with what he's doing in camp. >> Uh I don't I I again, I'm going through the tape right there. I didn't see it in the first couple plays. I saw once or twice, but it's really important to see him in the run game and see how he fares from that standpoint, especially against their first team, so it'll be great to see the rest of the film and see how he did, but you know, his talent is undeniable there from a pass rush standpoint, but we want to see his overall game. >> Scott Ronalds. >> Coach, I know you have four practices to get through this week, but um typically you've played your starters or at least some of them in the second preseason game. Is is that what you're leaning towards for right now but heading into this this week and your joint practices with the Chiefs obviously, but will you uh will you sprinkle in some starters or maybe give them a series or two? >> Yeah, I've been saying that the last two weeks. The healthy starters are going to play in week two. >> Do you know about how long? >> Not yet, no. >> Greg Auman. >> Hey Todd, I know in preseason so much uh is is when you come in and who you're with who you're up against. Um given what Jaylen showed in the second half last night, would you consider bringing him in ahead of Blaine Gabbert and having him get in earlier with with more higher-level players in this next game? >> Uh we'll watch the tape and we'll talk about it as a group. So we haven't gotten that far yet, but he did have a good ball game. >> I'm sorry if this was answered earlier. With Browning in his back, is it reasonable to think he might be in play to to play at home against the Chiefs or is that something you're more concerned about? >> We're hopeful. I'll see I'll see how he comes along during the week. >> Okay, Todd, thank you. >> Yeah. >> Anyone else? Good. >> That's all. Thanks Todd.

text: How's it going? Good. Fire away. Um, so it's just kind of kind of who we suited up and the numbers we had. Um, you know, and then I think in the second half we're we're in some second and long situations. I mean, he's he's a really young player who's got a bright future with a lot of room to grow. But that is why we drafted him is we thought he was an NFL quarterback. And I think we saw um a lot of talent that he was probably better than a seventh round pick, but he had an injury in college that we knew he wasn't going to be able to play much his first year. And so was his draft value maybe fell a little bit, but evaluating, we saw a guy who was an NFL thrower, who was very bright, who had the right size, and who knew had the chance to to be a player. Um and I think he's doing a good job. You know, I think um just kind of adjusting to Brock, adjusting to, like I said, our route tree and kind of learning the timing of things. It's new. It's it's new for any player, but he's doing a heck of a job. Mike's a really really smart guy. He is on it. He's out there competing and getting better. Um, you know, today we got him in one-on- ones. He ran some good routes, and I just I just like his growth every day. Um, and Mike has the right mindset that he's just out there to get better. He wants to make our team better. And and that's that's what it takes. I >> I think Mike, you know, he leads in his own way. He's he's naturally just kind of a a quiet guy. It goes about his work and and that's what we like about him a lot. He's he's all about what you do on the field and um so to me that's kind of what he is every day. It's how he shows up. title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 13 of 49ers Training Camp
text: The 49ers just finished day 13 of training camp. Here's who stood out. The good, wide receiver Mike Evans. He had his first dominant day of camp with the 49ers. To be fair, he missed about a week with a quad strain. Now he seems fully healthy and today he absolutely schooled Bernardo Green. More on him in a minute. First, Evans drew two defensive holding penalties on Green, one on a deep route and one in the end zone. Finally, Evans beat Green with a deep crossing route for a gain of 30. And then for good measure, Evans beat Deommodore Lenoir with a back shoulder fade during one-on-ones and a curl route during 11-on-11s. Good to see Evans slowly develop chemistry with Brock Purdy. The Niners need Evans to play like this all the time this year. Wide receiver D'Joun Smith. He mostly played with the starters after getting demoted to the second string offense on Saturday. Smith's best catch was a 15-yard gain over the middle after beating Lenoir with a dig route. He still doesn't create a ton of separation against man coverage, but neither does Evans. Both receivers are excellent at catching passes over the heads of defensive backs. And Smith in particular is fearless when it comes to running full speed across the field. It looks like he's being groomed to start this season considering he's not playing any special teams as opposed to Deebo Samuel, who's a punt returner and a kick returner. And when he plays with the starters, he mostly is a running back. Thank God. Wide receiver Malik Turner. He was the winner of the unofficial 30-year-old backup wide receiver who gets to play with the starters for a day award. Today, Turner beat Upton Stout deep to catch a 30-yard pass from Brock Purdy. In addition, Turner caught three passes from Mac Jones. Turner has been on the 49ers off and on since 2022 and has yet to catch a pass in a game, but now he's 30, so the Niners might want to play him this season. They love 30-year-old backups. Don't we all? Tight end Jake Tonges. He led all starters with three catches. Tonges clearly isn't the most dangerous receiver on the team, but he might be the most reliable one on the field in camp this year. Purdy clearly trusts him because Tonges usually finds a way to get open and come down with the ball when it's in his general vicinity. Expect him to make a significant, consistent impact this season. He's Purdy's go-to guy right now. Quarterback Brock Purdy, he continues to have by far the best camp of his career. He used to make at least one boneheaded decision per day, now he doesn't. Today he completed a no-look pass downfield to Jordan Watkins after freezing Jayden Dugar by staring right at him. That was cool. Later Purdy completed a 30-yard pass to Jacob Cowing. Seriously, who beat Deommodore Lenoir? Seriously. Purdy is tearing apart the Niners starting defense while throwing to backups most of the time. Good news for Purdy, embarrassing for Raheem Morris's defense. Quarterback Mac Jones, he completed a 40-yard deep pass to Deebo Samuel who beat Jack Jones. More on him in a minute. Mac Jones also threw two beautiful touchdown passes with anticipation in the red zone. Jones has had a rather nondescript camp so far, but this week is big for him because he most likely will start and play a lot this Thursday night against the Chargers. He needs to show that last season wasn't a fluke and that he really is a starting caliber quarterback, not someone like Trey Lance, the Chargers backup who will start against the Niners on Thursday. No pressure, Mac. Defensive end Nick Bosa, he made a rare appearance on a side field with the trainers which indicates that his knee tendinitis is real and getting better. I'm guessing he'll play week one in Australia against the Rams. I'm also guessing that this tendinitis will be an issue for Bosa the rest of the season and off and on for the rest of his career. Isn't getting old a drag? Safety Marqueise Seal, he made the most athletic play of the day. While in center field, he exploded toward the sideline and leaped to nearly intercept a deep pass from Purdy that was intended for Jacob Cowing. Ideally, it would have been nice to see Seal catch that ball. Still, he's the only safety on the roster who's fast enough to actually make a play on that pass from center field. He has a chance to become a quality starter. Cornerback Ifeanyi Odenigbo, he played exclusively with the third-stringers which is annoying because he never commits penalties or gives up big catches as opposed to Renardo Green and Jack Jones. Pryor should be starting opposite Lenoir. I'm guessing the Niners will figure that out soon enough. The not so good. Running back Christian McCaffrey. He didn't show up to practice and hasn't suited up in more than a week. I'm guessing his tightness is something more severe, possibly tendinitis. That's what Bosa has and the Niners initially said he was merely sore. Tendinitis sounds mild, but it cost McCaffrey eight games in 2024 and it never really goes away entirely. I'm guessing he'll play in the season opener, but I doubt he'll be full strength. Guard Dominic Puni. He missed practice with a concussion he apparently suffered yesterday. Without him, the Niners had zero starting caliber guards. Guard Carver Willis. He started at left guard and played so bad he got replaced by Connor Colby midway through practice even though Colby is awful, too. Willis just happens to be worse right now. He can't anchor whatsoever against a strong bull rush from a defensive tackle. Maybe that's because he played offensive tackle in college. Defensive tackle C.J. West. He left practice early with what appeared to be a head injury. The Niners really should trade for Vita Vea, but they won't even though they called the Buccaneers to check on his availability. I'm guessing the Niners offer is so low it's laughable. They love low balling teams. Defensive tackle Grayson Halton. He missed practice with an ankle injury. Can't blame this one on the substation. Cornerback Renardo Green. He got flagged twice for holding Mike Evans, once on a deep pass, once in the end zone. After the second penalty, Green walked over to the volunteer official who threw the flag and argued with him about the call. Instead of doing that, Green should stop holding receivers. He's playing his way out of the starting lineup. Cornerback Jack Jones. He's worse than Green. Jones gambles and intercepts the occasional pass, but he also gets burned all the time. Today he got beat deep by Deebo Samuel, which is hard to do in 2026. Green and Jones are competing for a starting spot and both are losing. Pryor is better than both of them. Someone tell the coaching
