text: Bombs away on that 49ers practice field. Both Brock Perie and M. Jones aired it out today and completed numerous deep passes, numerous different receivers as well. The usual suspects, Mike Evans, Dejon Stribbling made a lot of deep catches. But today, Malik Turner, the very good gunner for the 49ers, he had a couple of deep ones, including one where he was able to outmuscle Upton Stout for the football. And then there was Jacob Cowing, who I thought made a statement at today's practice. Speaking of a statement, George KD spoke afterwards and he believes that he can be ready for week one and he also has a return date to practice in mind. You know, like I've said, I have a chance. Uh, we're running around a lot, hitting top speeds. You know, hopefully we're back in pads practicing sooner than later. Um, you know, just trying to check the boxes and not be a dumbass is what I would say. >> Now, KD wouldn't share the exact practice return date that he has in mind, but we do know the exact game return date that he has in mind, and it is September 11th in Australia against the Rams. That would be 244 days after KD tore his Achilles against the Philadelphia Eagles in the playoffs. That would be quick. Yes, it'd be just over eight months, but not unprecedented even in 49ers history. Back in 2013, Michael Crabtree tore his Achilles in the off season and was back 183 days later, 6 and 1/2 months later. So, a month and a half faster for Crabtree than even the fastest possible return for George KD. It is possible, especially considering the work that George has been putting in. It started with what he said was some of the most boring rehab ever and has since gotten much more exciting as he has hit his top speeds over the course of the past couple of weeks. >> When when Elatro told me that I had a chance to play week one, as long as I took it, you know, did everything I was supposed to do, it was pretty easy to light a fire every single day. Um, but yes, no, it is the most boring rehab in the entire world. It's how many seated calf raises and standing and calf raises can you do in a day basically for 18 weeks. Much more from George KD in a little bit. Why don't we get to those practice highlights starting with Dre Green Law. What a sight that is to see him back in full pads for the 49ers. Not with the Denver Broncos here in 2026. Greenlaw doing a lot of individualized work. He's going to be ready for that season. Shout out to the duck that they served in the 49ers media room today. Gourmet meal. Now we take a look at Romelo Height with Sir Bosa in the background. Nick Bosa made an appearance on that 49ers practice field for the first time in a couple weeks coming back from the knee tendinitis and it looked like he was moving well in that side work. Here is the vet wide receiver treatment for both Mike Evans and look Dejon Stribbling. That is Andrew Hayes Stoker. 49ers assistant wide receivers coach during the special teams period making the vet wide receivers very comfortable with the 49ers playbook. There's CJ West. He's gotten I think even bulkier this year. CJ though went down with an injury later in practice today. Undisclosed at this point, but we'll keep an eye on CJ's status as we move back to Dre Green Law. Remember the last time this guy played a game in a 49ers uniform fully healthy? 2023. He was the best player on the field in that Super Bowl before he tore his Achilles running out onto the field. So should be a lot of excitement for Dre Green, especially considering the fact that the 49ers have some nice nice young linebackers. Jaden Duggar, Larry Worth playing behind him who are able to pick up some of the slack for Dre in case he has to miss a few snaps. And you know, it's an interesting defensive experiment for sure. We talk about some of those long long players for the 49ers. So, that was a look at the highlights of practice today. Now we get to hear a little bit from Klay Kubiaak talking about Brock Perie and the whole layer king comment that we heard from Raheem Morris just about a week ago. That's the nickname for Raheem Morris to Brock Birdie, the layer king. Klay Kubak thinks that Brock Pertie is the king of not just layered throws. He also thinks that Pertie has the ability to put some mustard on the football. There's a time and a place, but you want the mindset to drive the football. And um and Brock has both tools. And Brock is exceptional at whatever whatever layering it is. Uh throwing it over zoning defenders, um finding holes in the defense, he's exceptional at that. Um but what you want the mindset as a quarterback, I'm driving the football. And um you know, we we remind him of that and he has both tools. And so I think the nickname's funny. I appreciate it, but it's cool that Brock kind of takes it personally, too, and says, "No, I'm going to drive the ball. I'm not going to layer things. So, but you got to have both both tools in your bag. And so, it's it's kind of a funny deal between him and Raheem. >> Now, to Klay Kubak's point, Pertie has done a lot of everything in this training camp. He's driven the football. He has layered the football. He's placed it perfectly on those deep passes, the gimmies, the shorter passes, which are so important to success in the National Football League. He's been on the money with those. And we saw a bit of everything from Brock Perie today. Now, back to Jacob Cowing. Talked about him at the top of the show. We know that he's been out for a period of this training camp with the hip flexor injury, and we know that he hadn't been all too productive over the course of this training camp. A slow start for Jacob Cowing after he was very productive during OTAAS. Well, today there was a deep corner pattern. Brock Birdie threw the ball and this one was incomplete. Maris Seagull, the safety, and Jacob Cowing collided and Cowing went down and Cowing was down for a couple minutes and then he got up and he was limping and I thought that his practice was over and I was thinking here we go again. Jacob Cowing can't stay healthy. Been a lot of availability issues over the first couple seasons of his career. I guess the first three seasons of his career given the fact that the hip flexor kept him out of practice. But Cowing ended up returning. And not only did he return, I thought he made the best catch I've seen from him in a 49ers uniform. Just a 40-ard laser beam from Brock Birdie over the middle of the field. And Cowing had to at first he beat the defense. He was behind the safeties behind Upton Stout. He had to climb the ladder though to make the catch and he did an excellent job of doing just that. And I thought that it was a statement from Jacob Cowing, a statement of resilience and given some of the availability issues, a very necessary one. He might be the 49ers leader in the clubhouse at punt returner. Jordan Watkins, who was so good at wide receiver the other day in that 49ers preseason opener against Tennessee with those six catches, he's returned some punts in his career back at Miss, but he muffed one today and he was very upset with himself. And you know, it'd be great for the 49ers if Jordan Watkins wins both the Z receiver battle and the punt return battle, but they've got to make sure they put the best possible option at punt returner. And maybe that will be Jacob Cowing. I think that the 49ers, I've said this throughout all of camp, the guy's got insane speed, very, very fast. Availability has been the issue. Reliability has been the issue. and maybe today helped answer some of the questions about that availability and reliability in a positive way. Somebody who has been extremely reliable for the 49ers so far, unusually so for a rookie at that receiver position is Dejon Stribbling. And this is where we go back to George KD who Mike told me, texted me when KD was up at the podium today. KD can be a head coach like a college head coach maybe one day with how fiery he is. But gosh is he good with the media. Here's George KD on Dejon Stribbling. >> I love what Stribbling Now. My favorite thing about Stribb is actually just his mindset every single day. Like there's no ego at all. Um, and you know, one thing I love that Kyle does, he goes like, "Hey, like in front of the whole team, he's very good at like he will build you up and he'll also like point out your flaws." Hey strip, like you had like statistically you had a great game, you made great plays, but here's a couple plays that you know we need you to be great at and you weren't and like that led to bad run plays or you didn't like, hey, this route is a inside foot up, four step out route and you went outside foot up and you took five steps so the time of the play is messed up. who's like these little things you got to focus on and you know Strip didn't take offense to that. He looks at it as like all right well hey coaches give me an opportunity to get better and like that's the mindset you have to have and you got to be allowed to get coached and if you he's not sensitive whatsoever he's got the right mindset for everything and he shows up every day and I think he just works really really hard. >> It really sounds like Dejon Stribbling is the anti- Brandon Iayuk no ego. George KD seemed rather pointed with that part of his quote, but Stribbling making strides. You know, the 49ers, they'll they'll temper their compliments from for Dejan Stribbling when it comes from the coaching staff. I mean, just listen to this. >> Uh, I think he did a good job. Um, there's a lot for him to learn from that game. You know, there's there's things there's things from the game that I think everyone knows why we love him. the way he is with the ball in his hand, the way he catches the ball. He's very, very strong player, but there's things that he needs to keep working on. You know, the route running, the detail with alignment, all those things. It's going to get better with time, but he just needs to see it, see the reps, um, get better from the tape. But I was pleased with how he played. He made some good plays, and he's just got to keep growing, keep taking steps every week. >> Really evocative of Kyle Shanahan's appraisal of Dejon Stribbling. You know, said that he had a fine game, but pointed out that there were some issues on the first drive. So obviously the coaching staff wants to make sure that they're maximizing improvement and maximizing hunger from Dejon Stribbling, but the actions speak so loud. And when we see Dejon Stribbling next to Mike Evans during the special teams period, the 49ers have yanked Stribbling off of special teams. I mean, that's vet star receiver treatment that he's already getting. And I think that speaks volumes about what the 49ers believe they currently have with Dejon Stribbling. All right, more from practice today. This was some good news. Keon White, who's been out with the adductor injury at that defensive end position, he started hitting the sled today as part of his rehab. I can't film uh the rehab portion of of practice, but Keon White seemed to be hitting the sled with some vigor. I don't think that he's all too far from returning to practice. Mentioned that CJ West exited practice. So did Titus Leo. 49ers defensive end was signed as depth a couple of weeks ago. Titus Leo was shaken up after a play. Grayson Halton missed today's practice with an ankle issue. We're not sure how serious it is, but the rookie has been playing really, really well. We got some big- time compliments from Trent Williams yesterday. And Dominic Puny, 49ers top right guard, suffered a concussion, so he's in the protocol right now and he missed today's practice. Looking through some of the notes, I go back to one-on ones today. Enrique Cruz Jr., 49ers, fifth round draft pick, who was very raw coming in, offensive tackle, fastest tackle in the draft, but somebody was struggling just, you know, with the the small technicalities, which end up playing a very large role in O line success. Some of the hand usage, some of the ability to adjust to to moves and counter moves. Well, today he had his two best reps of one-on- ons. The first one really impressed Trent Williams who was watching intently from behind and we saw Agabo Aarono, veteran edge rusher, try to work against Enrique Cruz Jr. and when one move to the outside didn't work. He tried to spin and when he spun to the inside that didn't work either. And Trent Williams started clapping. Trent Williams is like, "Yeah, I could see that improvement from Enrique Cruz Jr." So I thought that was a big moment. We're a few weeks into training camp here. Today was actually the last camp session here at the 49ers facility with fans allowed. The next one against the Chargers is going to be the last one with fans period. That's going to be down in Elsaundo on Tuesday. But to see point A to point B the progress that Enrique Cruz Jr. has made. Maybe he won't be ready to play this year. But the 49ers are trying to develop a potential air apparent to Trent Williams. And he has mentioned already that Enrique Cruz Jr. acquires information very quickly and it does appear that he has taken some big big strides just if you look at those one-on-one drills over the course of this training camp. Luke Frell, speaking of strides, year two in the 49ers system, Luke Frell made a couple more catches today. That's been a theme of camp, Frell's rapport with Brock Pury in that 49ers offense. And George KD thinks that Frell is gonna have a big year. I think Luke's just having an absolutely stellar camp. I think he looks like a completely different player. Uh his confidence in the offense is fantastic and he's just out there making plays every single day. You know, he's running better. Um you know, that's what anybody that was like hard on Luke last year for, you know, maybe not living up to expectations. I'm just like, name one skilled player who's coming into our offense in year one and played at a high level. Like really, besides what, Emanuel Sanders in 2019 and maybe you can count Trent Williams. He's not really a skilled player even though he moves like one, but like everybody struggles in their first year because it's such a complex offense and what we require you to do as a tight end is everything. And so I think he just has the offense more under his belt. He has a better understanding of it. Gives him confidence to play fast and not think. And I think Luke's going to have a fantastic season this year. And that's big for the 49ers because even if KD's back for week one, say that he's on a little bit of a limited pitch count, the fact that Luke Ferrell has become a big part of the 49ers pass game over this training camp can really help pick up some slack. And theoretically, the 49ers could even run some 13 personnel. I mean, you speak of the Rams, that's their opponent week one. So, KD bullish on Frell, who definitely has been a much much bigger part of the 49ers past game over the course of this training camp. KD also gave us some insight into what Mike Evans is like in the 49ers locker room. >> I mean, anytime you had Mike Evans at the outside, it's not like they can really, you know, stuff the box because at any moment you can just throw a go ball. So, like most corners going to need help over the top. So, hopefully we're not really playing with eight to nine guys in the box in every single snap. I think that'll help. Um, yeah, but speed always helps because if the safeties have to be, you know, play a little bit deeper, they're not as quick to, you know, fill. And I think that'll just make it a little bit easier on our offensive line, our tight ends, our running back. Um, and then the more Brock gets comfortable with the offense and can get us out of, you know, bad run plays into a better run play or even a pass play, I think the run game is going to definitely take another step in the right direction this year and not be three-point yards. I mean, if it was hard, do y'all care? title: Training Camp Live: Sunday, August 16 | Pittsburgh Steelers

title: Big FIGHT, Elandon Roberts brings edge, DeShon Elliott returns, WR, OL shakeup | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all. This first Steelers practice today in full pads, they got their eighth installation in on both sides of the football. That means that they have now completed all eight. Um that is good. So, the playbook is fully put in. We'll see how much they can recall and actually do well with that. But, seems like the offense and defense are up to speed. So, let's talk about what happened today. Obviously, the big story of today that most of you probably have heard about is brawl, fight, melee, whatever you want to call it. It was definitely the biggest skirmish of camp thus far. Um it kind of started on Robert Spillane and Jennings hit on Maxx Williams near the pylon. Williams took exception to it. Tight end Lance Mason didn't like it. Spillane and Jennings had talked a lot of trash throughout the day. Um there was a play a few plays earlier where ball was intended for Williams and Spillane and Jennings broke it up. And it seems like that just boiled over. And then, more and more players came running over, especially Deshaun Elliott. Uh he got into this with Jaheem Bell, one of the tight ends. And it just felt like that there was tension in this practice. This was the most physical practice of training camp so far. And a large portion of that was due to one, the defensive backs talking a lot of smack. Um Brandon Echols and Damontae Kazee did not practice and they talked a lot. Um but, even the guys that were playing uh talked a ton today. Spillane and Jennings, Damontae Kazee, Antoine Brooks, etc. Uh Ahkello Witherspoon, you know, all these guys were talking a lot of smack. And then, number two, and I think the main culprit, Atlanta Roberts, the Steelers' new linebacker that they resigned uh earlier this week. This guy came in and he hit Travis Homer big on a third tempo. Um he just decked Levi Wallace at one point. Decked Caleb Johnson. Mason McCormick at one point was trash talking and saying, "Pipe down, fresh legs." E Rob responded with a few more hits and physicality. I think you could see DeShawn Elliott feeding off of DeShawn Elliott, by the way. Back, full participant for the first time in training camp. It seems like 25 is fully back. He took first team reps in team today. But, E Rob is such a spark plug, and he wouldn't straight-out admit it uh to me, but you could tell. If you know how to read E Rob, he was trying to get the intensity going here. Um so, that was something that obviously happened, and I think added some intensity to the Steelers practice today. Um there were other things that happened. I thought Roman Wilson looked really good. Um you know, no DK Metcalf or Michael Pittman again. No Brandon Smith. Cade Weishuhn was back. That was good, you know, Weishuhn did miss yesterday. Luckily for the Steelers, they got uh their rookie back. But, I thought Roman Wilson back in the slot today looked really good. Um Jeremy Bernard had a really nice diving touchdown in the seven-on-seven, but also a false start in the red zone drill. And then, a a on the last play, they tried to like run some like special spread-out flip back to Bernard, and he wasn't looking for it. Rodgers clearly was a little frustrated with that. So, we'll see, but I thought Roman Wilson had another good day. Has to translate onto the football field. Jeremy Bernard had a really good game, but uh that will be something to watch. I think Peyton Wilson continues to play really really good football. Um this guy in the team run periods had at least three or four TFLs today. He continues to just go up up up up up. You can't help but be impressed by Peyton Wilson. Um I think he's going to be the starting linebacker next to Patrick Queen. We'll see how much, but the run-down production so encouraging to see from him. One guy I think that is kind of forcing his way out of this team because I think you kind of need to respect what he's doing is Robert Tonyan. Tonyan continues to just flash in camp, make good catches over the middle of the field. He's a special teamer. Riley Nowalkowski has done that too, but you saw his versatility today. Both of those guys, they ran like a full house package where essentially they had two tight ends sometimes in the backfield, offset different things that they would do and both those guys were in there. Um D'Wayne Washington got in on there. Even Broderick Jones at some points where you know where was in the backfield. It was kind of interesting. They mixed and matched a lot of combos. But I thought the Steelers clearly trying to experiment with some run game looks. They also were experimenting with some O-line combos. We saw more Brock Hoffman, more Broderick Jones with the first team today. Still slightly more towards Anderson and Cook. Um in terms of injuries, no Maxi Hanocho, no DK Metcalf, no Michael Pittman, no Brandin Smith. Israel Mukuamu who got hurt yesterday did not practice today. Um we will see where some of these other Brandon Echols, T'Quan Breeceker continue to be held out as well. Um so the Steelers are are banged up. Sebastian Joseph Day was out. Um but at least one positive thing, Sean Elliott's back. Um and and that's really important for the Steelers in that safety room. They got a little healthier there. Steven Sims didn't take as many first team reps. He had a rough day anyways. I know he had a really good Thursday. Um but did did struggle today and I think he's had a little bit of an up and down training camp. But all right folks, make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn on the notification bell for more and thanks for watching. I'll be back tomorrow.
